merged.title: A world step that throws used to be committed half-done; the atomic fix is uncommitted, failures still freeze the game silently, and loadAndResume still adopts a half-simulated catch-up
merged.summary: At HEAD and on the live site (0d9fc5a), mutateFast published the half-stepped working copy when its recipe threw. stepOnce advances the clock last, so a throw in a late subsystem (market, staff, visitors, progression, shows) committed stepped tanks with the clock frozen; the 250 ms loop re-stepped the same window, animals starved at a frozen hour and autosave saved it (probe: 40 ticks, clock +0 h, 15 deaths, autosaved). The uncommitted working tree makes mutateFast atomic (resetFastMutate on throw), keeps the failed tick's hours in the backlog and adds core-fastmutate-atomic.test.ts. Still open: a deterministic fault now freezes the world with no player-facing signal (speed stays at 10x, one console message, loopStats.errors only via __AQ.stats()); loadAndResume runs simulateOffline on the loaded object in place and, on a throw, installs the half-simulated state (its comment ‘keep the loaded state as-is’ is false); the new test only faults before any tank has stepped.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) Commit the in-tree fastMutate/GameLoop change and its test after an independent review. 2) loadAndResume: simulate a copy, `const work = structuredClone(state); summary = simulateOffline(work, elapsed); state = work;`; on a throw keep the decoded state untouched, delete offlineGrace and toast “Offline catch-up failed; resuming where you left off.” 3) runTick: count consecutive failed ticks (reset on success); after 3, pause through `useGame.getState().mutate(d => { d.clock.speed = 0 })` inside its own try and show a persistent danger banner (“The simulation hit an error and is paused. Your last save is intact.” with Export a copy and Reload); see the tick-failure owner question. 4) Extend core-fastmutate-atomic.test.ts: a fault injected after the tanks step (force stepProgression or stepShows to throw) leaves clock and tanks unchanged; a loadAndResume case whose adopted state deep-equals the decoded save; the 3-failure pause. 5) PlacementGhost.tsx:254-269: move the try/catch outside `useGame.getState().mutate(...)` so a throw after `spend` discards the purchase, matching src/ui/common/actions.ts:46-48.

merged.title: A future schema bump would let the deployed v0.4.0 code restore an older backup and overwrite the newer save, and the save-compatibility rules disagree
merged.summary: The live v0.4.0 code treats a save with schemaVersion > 1 as damaged (‘too_new’), falls back to the slot's older .backup, tells the player the save was damaged, and its next two autosaves rotate out and overwrite the newer record (reproduced on a memory backend). Deployed code can't be patched, so only policy prevents this. The rules conflict: design §3.3/§21 forbid a bump and require ‘a v0.4.0 save loads with no repairs’ after every phase; master §3.5 and ADR-0001 make compatibility best-effort and allow a bump. The S0 revision added an interim SCHEMA_BUMP owner gate and ACTIVE requirements PERSIST-001 (v0.4.0 save loads with repairs: [] at every slice) and PERSIST-003 (no bump; a too-new save is never replaced), which go further than ADR-0001 without the owner's approval; PERSIST-003 has no test. The stale-tab guard only protects a v0.4.0 tab that saw the newer write in the same session.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides the schema policy (P1 question); record the answer verbatim in an ADR that supersedes the master §3.5 note and confirms or relaxes PERSIST-001/003. Whatever the answer: 1) implement PERSIST-003 in the 0.5 code now (contained, core persistence): in loadGameDetailed a copy that decodes as too_new is final (return code ‘too_new’, never fall back to .backup or another backend's copy); in saveGame/isIntact never rotate or overwrite a record whose header or body schemaVersion exceeds SCHEMA_VERSION; test with a schemaVersion-2 primary plus a v1 backup on a memory backend (load returns too_new without restoring, saveGame refuses). 2) Commit a real v0.4.0 fixture save generated at 0d9fc5a for PERSIST-001's test. 3) If a bump is ever approved: write v2 under a new key prefix and leave v1 keys untouched, ship the too_new-final build first, and test that v0.4.0 can't destroy v2 data; define ‘locally reversible’ as throwaway browser profiles or origins for QA.

merged.title: Agent-written files can still stand in for owner authority: approval references, ‘Accepted’ ADRs and protected-file updates aren't verified, and ADR-0003 itself awaits ratification
locations: AGENTS.md (Don't edit the rules that judge you)
merged.summary: The committed harness never said who the owner is or how an approval is recorded, and agents could edit the rules that judge them. The S0 revision added OPERATIONS §2 (an approval is the owner's own words in a top-level session, recorded verbatim in an ADR plus an owner-decision ledger event), an ‘Owner approval’ block in the ADR template, and protect.mjs. Still open: ADR-0002:90-91 says a fresh agent may rely on a decision recorded in ‘an ADR, the master or STATE.json’, contradicting §2; check-state only checks that remoteApproval/multiplayerApproval paths exist, and protect.mjs --update accepts any existing ADR file, so an agent-written ADR can re-sign any protected change; PROTECTED.json doesn't exist yet, so the protectedFiles gate can't pass and the AGENTS.md protection rule is unenforced; the ledger append-only check compares only with HEAD, so a committed rewrite passes; the orchestrator prompt still says ‘repair stale agent documentation’ and ‘prune obsolete context’. ADR-0003 is marked Accepted and changes the master, OPERATIONS, AGENTS and the prompts on the strength of the general ‘improve it’ request, while its own §10 says those need verbatim owner approval.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) Ask the owner to ratify ADR-0003 (P1 question); record the answer verbatim in ADR-0004 and, until then, describe ADR-0003 in INDEX.md as ‘Accepted, pending owner ratification at S0-T12’. 2) In ADR-0004, supersede ADR-0002's last consequence with: “A fresh agent may rely on an owner decision only when the owner's own words are recorded verbatim in an ADR with a matching owner-decision ledger event (OPERATIONS.md §2). STATE.json flags only mirror such an ADR; they are never approvals.” 3) check-state.mjs: remoteApproval and multiplayerApproval must name an ADR under docs/agent/decisions whose Status is Accepted, whose ‘## Owner approval’ section is non-empty, and which an owner-decision ledger event cites. 4) protect.mjs --update: refuse an ADR that isn't Accepted; for the master, OPERATIONS, README_FIRST, AGENTS, CLAUDE, the prompts and owner-decision ADRs require a non-empty ‘## Owner approval’ block; for templates and scripts/agent require a recorded review in evidence/<slice>/reviews/ that names the diff; treat a change to PROTECTED.json or protect.mjs itself as an owner gate. 5) validateLedger: also require the ledger at `git show <lastAcceptedCheckpoint ?? actualBaselineSha>:docs/agent/LEDGER.jsonl` to be a byte prefix. 6) Create PROTECTED.json at S0-T12 under the owner-ratified ADR so the owner sees the initial hashes. 7) Orchestrator prompt (owner-approved): line 24 → “repair stale factual fields (SHA, branch, status, paths) in STATE, HANDOFF and CURRENT_SLICE; requirements, acceptance criteria and rules change only through an ADR”; line 91 → “prune obsolete chat and tool context; never delete files under docs/agent/”. Add agent.test.mjs cases (a self-written ADR without an approval block is refused). Local records can't stop deliberate forgery; the owner's review of protected-file changes at each boundary and the remote guards are the real backstop.

merged.title: Fresh-context rollover is defined but not enforced: no rule for auto-compaction, no measurable early-rollover trigger, and the bootstrap assertion is optional
merged.summary: The owner's harness required a fresh context after every slice plus automatic advance, which one Claude Code session can't do. ADR-0002 decision 3, KICKOFF.md, relaunch.mjs and OPERATIONS §1 now say the session ends at the boundary and the owner (or the opt-in launcher) starts the next; bootstrap-check.mjs validates a fresh session's assertion and refuses the session that closed the previous slice. Remaining: nothing says what to do after Claude Code auto-compacts a session, although a compaction summary is exactly the ‘agent summary’ master §0 forbids relying on; the 65% early-rollover trigger in §17 can't be measured from inside a session and has no observable proxy; nothing requires a passing bootstrap assertion before BOOTSTRAP → BASELINE_VERIFY, and the freshness check is silently skipped when the closing NEXT_SLICE event recorded no session id.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) Add to OPERATIONS §1 and the KICKOFF prompt (ADR): “If this conversation was compacted or summarised, treat yourself as a fresh agent: finish the current stable point, run the master §17 rollover checklist, commit locally and end the session.” 2) Add to OPERATIONS §1 observable early-rollover proxies: an auto-compaction happened; an S3 internal checkpoint was committed; a second failed repair loop on one defect. Keep master §14 unchanged. 3) record-event.mjs: refuse BOOTSTRAP → BASELINE_VERIFY unless docs/agent/evidence/<slice>/bootstrap-*.json exists and bootstrap-check passes; stamp the session id on NEXT_SLICE from currentSession() and refuse the event when it is null. 4) bootstrap-check.mjs fails, rather than skips, when either session id is missing. 5) check-state: a slice past BOOTSTRAP without a passing bootstrap assertion is an error. Add agent.test.mjs cases; scripts are protected, so this needs an ADR and an independent reviewer's sign-off.

merged.title: State machine, gate keys and bookkeeping are mostly reconciled; check-state still requires only 6 of the 11 gates and the YELLOW sentence contradicts itself
merged.summary: As committed, the legal-state list lacked MULTIPLAYER_READINESS_GATE (used by the S4 flow), nothing reached COMPLETE_LOCAL, NEXT_SLICE, OWNER_GATE and BLOCKED_MANUAL_REVIEW had no exits, STATE lacked the diff-hygiene and requirements-audit gates, statuses had no vocabulary, the ledger was empty and STATE's baseline and branch were null. The S0 revision fixed nearly all of it: OPERATIONS §4's transition table (mirrored in lib.mjs and enforced by record-event), any state → OWNER_GATE with ownerGateReason and resumeState, STATE schema 2 with 11 gate keys, defined statuses, a seeded ledger, and the baseline and branch recorded. Remaining: check-state.mjs:96 requires only typecheck, unit, build, e2e, diffCheck and independentReview, so deleting harnessTests, requirementsAudit, testInventory or protectedFiles from STATE lets acceptance pass without them; master §26 still says YELLOW needs owner approval ‘if it changes owner-visible behavior’ while the next sentence and OPERATIONS §2 make every unrepaired YELLOW an owner decision; the manifest template's checkpointSha can never be filled inside the checkpoint commit it identifies; the meaning of slice ‘ALL’ is implicit.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) lib.mjs: export REQUIRED_GATES (all 11 keys); check-state requires every key (browserQa may be NOT_APPLICABLE) and verify-slice and OPERATIONS §6 use the same list; add an agent.test.mjs case where removing requirementsAudit fails. 2) Master §26 (owner ADR, after the YELLOW question): replace the YELLOW paragraph with “`YELLOW` never advances on its own. It becomes `GREEN` through a repair and a fresh `GREEN` re-review, or through an owner-approved ADR that lists each accepted limitation (owner gate `YELLOW_VERDICT:<slice>`).” and make OPERATIONS §2 say the same. 3) Remove checkpointSha from EVIDENCE_MANIFEST_TEMPLATE.json and emptyManifest, or document it as always null: the checkpoint is identified by its tag and STATE.lastAcceptedCheckpoint, the evidence by codeTree. 4) Add to OPERATIONS §5 or REQUIREMENTS.json's rule: “Slice ALL marks a standing constraint (status ACTIVE); the requirements audit checks it for violations, never for completion.”

merged.title: Repair-stop rule: tightened in §3.3 and OPERATIONS §5, but §11.2 and §31 still state the old rule and a defect can be re-filed to reset its counters
merged.summary: Originally only ‘materially different’ attempts counted, judged by the repairer, with one global counter, no defect key, no root-cause path and no exit from BLOCKED_MANUAL_REVIEW. Now there are per-defect ids, every attempt is logged, a reviewer judges distinctness, a 3-distinct/5-total cap applies, a root-cause path and an ADR exit exist. Still open: master §11.2 (‘A materially different repair strategy increments repairAttempt’; ‘At 3 failed materially-different repair attempts’) and §31 (‘Three materially different failed repairs → manual stop’) state the old rule, and OPERATIONS says the master wins a conflict; defect ids are free-form, so the same failing gate or test can be filed under a new id and its counters restart; validateRepairCount checks only the current target and only that the ledger count isn't above STATE's; an oscillation (§32) counts nothing; context-pack omits repairTarget and repairTotalAttempts.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) Owner-approved ADR: master §11.2 → “Every repair attempt is counted per defect (OPERATIONS.md §5). A reviewer, not the repairer, judges whether a strategy is materially different. At 3 distinct strategies or 5 attempts in total on one defect, write evidence/<slice>/root-cause-<defect>.md and move to BLOCKED_MANUAL_REVIEW.” §31 → “3 distinct strategies or 5 attempts on one defect → manual stop (OPERATIONS.md §5).” 2) Repair events carry `source` (the gate plus the failing test id or review-finding id); validateRepairCount counts events by source across all defect ids, requires the logged count to equal repairTotalAttempts for the target, and errors when a new repairTarget has the source of a defect whose gate never went GREEN. 3) OPERATIONS §5: “An oscillation (fixing A breaks B and back) counts as an attempt against both defects.” 4) context-pack.mjs includes repairTarget and repairTotalAttempts. Add agent.test.mjs cases.

merged.title: The requirements registry doesn't yet cover the approved scope: umbrella ids with vacuous criteria, no ACC/PLAT/DES/PERF/CONST entries, and no check that catches dropped or reworded scope
merged.summary: At 94de6bb the registry had 11 rows with 4 of the 9 required fields and 6 of 15 families in use. Schema 2 now has 23 ids with source, acceptance, tasks, tests and evidence, defined statuses, append-only ids checked against HEAD, and new HARNESS, REL, PERSIST and SOC entries; the decomposition (S0-T6) is in progress. Still: NAV-001, MKT-001 and the other originals are umbrellas whose only criterion (‘Every NAV requirement sourced from … is GREEN’) is vacuous while no child exists, and no script checks that children exist; there are no ACC, PLAT, DES, PERF or CONST entries, so design §18 accessibility, §19 test ids, the Copy-link and notification platform seams, performance budgets and the master §3 owner constraints trace to nothing; deliverables absent from master §9's lists (the dock-width fix and dock-width.spec, the Supplies AWC row, GameEvent.offerId) have no slice owner; requirements-audit never compares the registry with master §9 bullets or design sections; only id deletion against HEAD is detected, so a weakened acceptance string passes and a committed deletion passes on the next run.
merged.recommendedFix: Finish S0-T6 with these rules. 1) One requirement per master §9 S1-S4 bullet and per normative design subsection (§5-§19), §21 ‘Done when’ item and §20.3 planned test change (naming the exact test and assertion changed); tests go in `tests`, not separate ids. Keep the 11 umbrella ids; children cite them in `source`. Families: DES (including test-id areas; dock-width fix → S4, Supplies AWC row → S3-A, GameEvent.offerId → S3-B), PLAT (Copy link/share and notification seams), ACC (design §18 per surface, testable), PERF (BLOCKED, ‘budget: owner to set’; never invented), CONST (master §3 owner constraints, ACTIVE). Design-optional items (§6.6 share sheet, §9.2 forecast meters, §10.4 ‘Automation gear’ row) become DEFERRED with an ADR reference unless the owner promotes them. 2) requirements-audit.mjs: past PLAN_LOCK, fail when an umbrella of the current slice has no child, or when a current-slice master §9 bullet, a design heading (minus an explicit exemption list: sections in DESIGN_REGISTRY overriddenBy plus Contents and the Glossary), a §19 test-id area or a §20 test file is cited by no requirement. 3) validateRequirements: also compare with `git show <lastAcceptedCheckpoint ?? actualBaselineSha>:docs/agent/REQUIREMENTS.json`; fail when an old id's description, source or any old acceptance string changed or vanished without a `decision` reference (appending criteria stays allowed). 4) The independent requirements reviewer confirms coverage before S0 acceptance (already a criterion). Add agent.test.mjs cases.

merged.title: S0's contract is now complete and testable; the master still calls the S0 scripts ‘Recommended’ and makes rollover part of ‘done’
merged.summary: At 94de6bb CURRENT_SLICE.md had seven tasks, no acceptance criteria, cited no requirement and left out four of the fourteen S0 deliverables, and the S0 builder writes the checkers that later grade S0. The working tree rewrote it from the template: governing requirements, a task table S0-T1..T12 mapped to requirement ids, testable acceptance criteria, required reviewers (code-architecture and security-data), and an owner review before acceptance (S0-T12); bootstrap-check.mjs gives the bootstrap test a pass criterion. Residual: master §41 is still headed ‘Recommended helper scripts’ although §9 says S0 includes them; §47's ‘fresh-context rollover performed’ reads like an acceptance precondition although rollover happens after ACCEPT; and because S0 builds its own judges, acceptance depends on reviewers actually exercising the negative fixtures.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) Owner-approved ADR: rename master §41 to “Required S0 helper scripts”; reword §47's bullet to “the session ended at HANDOFF and the next session's bootstrap-check.mjs passed (OPERATIONS.md §1)”. 2) In CURRENT_SLICE.md S0-T10, require the code-architecture and security-data reviewers to run `node --test 'scripts/agent/*.test.mjs'` themselves and to try at least three hand-made bad fixtures against check-state.mjs (a GREEN gate without evidence, a rewritten ledger line, a changed protected file), recording the commands in their reports.

merged.title: Independent review: reviews aren't tied to the code they reviewed, reviewer triggers are the orchestrator's judgement, and the context pack still feeds reviewers the handoff
merged.summary: Fixed in the working tree: a reviewer mode in AGENTS.md, reviewer-written report files ending in a Verdict line, read-only roles, an adversarial role, a new reviewer instance after every repair (OPERATIONS §7, CLAUDE.md), and check-state requiring the last review per required role to be GREEN. Still open: check-state never compares a review's codeTree with the accepted tree (it does for command gates), so a GREEN review from before a repair satisfies ACCEPT; required reviewers, browserQa applicability and specialist triggers are set by the orchestrator, browserQa NOT_APPLICABLE is accepted without checking the diff, and the security-data trigger is worded by topic, so S1's deep-link boot or S2's additive save fields can be argued out of it; ‘adversarial’ is a role but not a required one; context-pack.mjs says it builds packs for builders and reviewers but always includes HANDOFF, contradicting OPERATIONS §7.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) check-state validateGateEvidence: for independentReview and each role in requiredReviewers, the newest GREEN review must have codeTree equal to the target tree (error when acceptance is claimed, warning otherwise), as for command gates; add an agent.test.mjs case with a stale review. 2) Derive triggers from `git diff --name-only <lastAcceptedCheckpoint ?? actualBaselineSha>` plus untracked files: browser-qa for src/ui/**, src/render/**, index.html, public/**, *.css; security-data for src/persistence/**, src/state/**, src/types/game.ts, src/game/fastMutate.ts, src/game/useAutosave.ts, src/game/GameLoop.tsx, public/**, index.html, new localStorage or IndexedDB keys, scripts/agent/** and .claude/**; performance for src/render/**, src/ai/**, src/runtime/**, src/game/** and src/sim/world.ts. Error at acceptance when a triggered role is missing from requiredReviewers, or browserQa is NOT_APPLICABLE while UI paths changed, unless an ADR waives it. Write the same list into OPERATIONS §7 with: “security-data is required for any change to what is saved or how it is loaded, schema bump or not.” 3) Add ‘adversarial’ to the roles check-state requires before ACCEPT and to OPERATIONS §7's required roles. 4) context-pack.mjs --reviewer: omit HANDOFF and LEDGER; include the contract, the requirement subset, cited design headings, `git diff <base>..` with untracked files and the evidence paths. Optional: record a promptSha256 with each review and hash CURRENT_SLICE's acceptance criteria at PLAN_LOCK. No local mechanism can stop an orchestrator writing a review itself; the owner's audit of report files is the backstop.

merged.title: Evidence now has a layout, hashes and code-tree binding, but browser-QA runs aren't tied to the build they saw and ignored inputs sit outside the code tree
merged.summary: At 94de6bb nothing said where evidence lives or how it is hashed, `*.log` silently excluded evidence logs, and nothing tied a gate result to its code. Now evidence logs are committed (`!docs/agent/evidence/**/*.log`), logs, reports and screenshots carry SHA-256, every record carries a codeTree, check-state re-hashes cited files and refuses ignored evidence, and a checkpoint-plus-bookkeeping-commit procedure exists. Remaining: browser runs record the recording checkout's codeTree, but check-state only requires browserRuns to be non-empty and never compares it, and dev-server QA can't prove which build it saw (vite.config.ts stamps ‘dev’ outside builds; gitSha ignores uncommitted changes); git-ignored inputs (.env*.local, node_modules) can influence a gate without changing codeTree; Playwright failure screenshots and traces in test-results/ are wiped by the next run and never copied.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) check-state: when acceptance is claimed, the latest browserRun's codeTree must equal the accepted tree. 2) capture-evidence --browser: require `--url` and `--build-id` (read from /version.json or __BUILD_ID__); acceptance browser QA runs against `npm run build && npx vite preview --port <own> --strictPort` on the candidate tree and refuses a dirty tree. 3) runAndRecord: add an `inputs` fingerprint (hashes of package-lock.json and node_modules/.package-lock.json, plus a flag when any .env*.local exists); check-state compares it with the accepted run. 4) verify-slice: after an e2e run, copy test-results/** into .agent-runs/evidence/<slice>/e2e-<stamp>/ and record hashes. Add agent.test.mjs cases (scripts are protected: ADR plus reviewer sign-off).

merged.title: E2E server reuse is now opt-in, but a stray E2E_REUSE can still leak into gate runs, the port and server aren't recorded, and dev/QA servers drift ports
merged.summary: The committed config reused any server on port 4399 (`reuseExistingServer: true`), so a gate could pass against another worktree's or a stale preview's code while the evidence recorded this checkout's code tree. The working tree makes reuse opt-in (E2E_REUSE=1), forbids .only, and OPERATIONS §8 asks for one E2E_PORT per worktree. Remaining: the gate run passes the shell environment through, so an E2E_REUSE=1 left in an agent's shell makes a gate reuse whatever is listening; E2E_PORT and the reuse flag aren't recorded; `npm run dev` (port 5173, strictPort false) silently moves to another port and origin, with other saves, when 5173 is busy (it currently runs this checkout's long-lived dev server); concurrent agent runs load the CPU during perf measurements.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) verify-slice.mjs: run the e2e gate with `env: { E2E_REUSE: '' }` so a gate never reuses a server, and record E2E_PORT and the reuse flag in the manifest record; classify a busy-port failure as environment, not a repair attempt. 2) Derive a per-worktree default port in verify-slice (e.g. 4400 + hash(ROOT) % 500) and pass it as E2E_PORT. 3) OPERATIONS §8: “Browser QA starts its own server with `npx vite --host 127.0.0.1 --port <own> --strictPort` (or `vite preview … --strictPort`) and records that URL in the evidence; never use a server another session started.” Leave `npm run dev` unchanged for the owner. 4) Optional: a lock file under .agent-runs/ that verify-slice takes for e2e and perf runs. Add an agent.test.mjs case for (1).

merged.title: Design overrides are listed in ADR-0003, but the design registry, the context pack and the master's own S3-B wording don't carry them to agents who read a section
merged.summary: The design spec called itself the single source of truth and asserted rules the master overrides (no schema bump, lane sign-off, a 0.5.0 release step, production ships last, open question 5). The working tree added a banner to the spec, ADR-0003's 11-row supersession table and a 5-row overriddenBy list in DESIGN_REGISTRY. Gaps: the registry and ADR-0003 disagree (the registry lacks §3.5's mutation and RNG lines, §1 item 10, the §21 per-phase v0.4.0-save gate, D3 and option C, §22 risks 1, 5 and 9, the D7/D13/§12.7 deferral and the §12.3 iOS copy); context-pack.mjs prints cited design headings without their overrides, so a builder or reviewer who loads only a section still reads it as normative; master §48 needs every superseded behaviour checkable against an approved record; master S3-B says ‘fixed 10 PM–8 AM quiet hours’ and ADR-0001 ‘Quiet hours fixed at 22:00–08:00’, both omitting the on/off switch (default on, notify-quiet) that master §3.10 and design §12.2-§12.3 keep (ADR-0003's row clarifies it).
merged.recommendedFix: 1) Make DESIGN_REGISTRY.json overriddenBy match ADR-0003's table row for row, adding: “§3.5 ‘only simRng’ and ‘all changes via useGame.mutate’ → master §5”; “§1 item 10 → master §3.5, PERSIST-001, PERSIST-003”; “§21 per-phase ‘a v0.4.0 save loads with no repairs’ → PERSIST-001 (kept as a standing gate)”; “D3 → ADR-0001 option C, DESIGN-S3D”; “§22 risk 9 ‘can slip to 0.6’ → master §9”; “§22 risk 1 → open owner question”; “§12.3 iOS ‘add to Home Screen’ copy → open owner question (master §44)”; “D7 lock-screen part, D13 native part, §12.7, Phase 6, notify-forecast.test.ts → DEFERRED (master §3.10)”. 2) context-pack.mjs prints the overriddenBy rows for every cited design section (with a test); check-state warns when the registry and ADR-0003's table disagree. 3) Owner-approved ADR: master S3-B bullet → “fixed 10 PM–8 AM quiet hours with an on/off switch (default on, `notify-quiet`); hours not editable in 0.5”. Don't edit ADR-0001; ADR-0003's row is the clarification. Leave the approved spec's body untouched.

merged.title: The written mutation, render-write and RNG rules still don't match the code in AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, LANES.md, the design spec and game.ts
merged.summary: The committed rules said every state change goes through useGame.mutate and randomness comes only from ctx.rng/simRng; the code also writes through mutateFast and setGame and keeps persisted subsystem streams. The working tree fixed AGENTS.md, master §5 and ARCHITECTURE.md:34-35 for the main points. Still inaccurate: mutateFast is listed for ‘the game loop and offline catch-up’ only, but it also runs the pre-save flush (session.ts:38,75) and dev time-advance; setGame is listed for ‘load or new game’, but fixture and showcase boot, dev tools, sandboxes and window.__AQ use it too; AGENTS.md's ‘Rendering never writes game state’ contradicts eleven render-side input handlers that commit player actions through mutate (the master's ‘never mutates game state directly’ is right); ‘useGame.mutate (UI and AI actions)’ licenses frame-rate-dependent AI writes, while ARCHITECTURE.md:24 says AI ‘writes runtime’ and the one real AI write is TankAI's observed:* tutorial flag; keyed mulberry32(hashString(…)) streams aren't mentioned; game.ts:3 still says ‘The ONLY way … is mutate(...)’, LANES.md:50,53 and design §3.5 keep the old wording, and ARCHITECTURE.md:32 and LANES.md:46 say species are read through getSpecies() although findSpecies is used in about 75 files.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner-approved ADR (AGENTS.md and the master are protected): replace AGENTS.md's determinism bullet, and mirror it in master §5, with: “Keep the simulation deterministic (OPERATIONS.md §11). In src/sim, randomness comes only from `simRng(state)` / `ctx.rng`, a subsystem's own persisted stream (`staff.rng`, `shows.rng`; new subsystems get their own), or a keyed `mulberry32(hashString(…))` stream derived from the seed and entity ids; never `Math.random`, the wall clock or render state. Persistent game state changes only through the store boundary: `useGame.mutate` (player actions from UI and render input handlers), `mutateFast` (the game loop, offline catch-up, the pre-save flush and dev time-advance) and `setGame` (replacing the whole world: new game, load, fixture or showcase boot, dev tools). Per-frame and draw code (`useFrame`, AI steps, materials) never writes game state; the one per-frame write is TankAI's `observed:*` tutorial flag, and any other needs an ADR.” Then (repo docs): src/state/game.ts:3 header and ARCHITECTURE.md:34 get the same three-path text; ARCHITECTURE.md:24 → “src/ai per-frame creature behaviour (reads sim state, writes runtime; its only game-state write is the tutorial `observed:*` flag via `useGame.mutate`)”; ARCHITECTURE.md:32 and LANES.md:46 → “Species facts live only in src/data/species. Read them through the registry in src/data/species/index.ts (`getSpecies` throws on an unknown id, `findSpecies` returns undefined, `listSpecies`); branch on data fields, never on species ids or names.”; LANES.md:50,53 point to ARCHITECTURE.md; design §3.5 is overridden through the registry (M12), not edited.

merged.title: Release and version: the interim rule (stay at 0.4.0, notes under ## Unreleased, REL-003) is in place, but the registry and repo docs still point at the old release step

merged.title: Design §6's router assumes panel targets and shell state the code doesn't have: Back can't leave a sub-view, Settings tabs never reach the URL, and the More sheet would close itself
merged.summary: §6.2 maps #/shop, #/encyclopedia and #/livestock to existing ‘tab:’ targets, but MarketPanel's tab handler never clears offerId, Encyclopedia's leaves speciesId and article, and Livestock has no target back to Animals (ShowsPanel does this right), so Back from an offer or species page leaves it on screen and a stale useNav.sub can push the sub-view URL back. §6.3 subscribes the URL to useShell.settingsTab, but SettingsPanel consumes and clears it at once and keeps the visible tab in local state, so tab clicks never reach the URL and a cleared value would rewrite #/settings/<tab> to #/settings; the tank card's useTankCardTab.want behaves the same. More as a useShell popover would be closed by GameHUD's global pointerdown and Escape rules unless its root is an .ag-popover, and POPOVER_TRIGGER has no ‘more’ entry for focus return; §18 credits usePopoverFocusReturn for panels, which actually use PanelHost's lastFocus. Nothing reaches players yet; it is a spec gap for S1.
merged.recommendedFix: Record as S1 design errata in docs/agent/BACKLOG.md and the S1 contract (per the errata-process question): 1) “A route with no sub-view segment closes any open sub-view.” applyRoute always sends an explicit root target (#/livestock → tab:animals, #/encyclopedia → tab:species); each panel's tab: handler clears its sub-view state (Market: offerId, wizard, focusListing; Encyclopedia: speciesId, article; Livestock gains tab:animals, tab:young, tab:past, tab:production) and its useNav.sub entry inside the re-entrancy guard. 2) Settings and the tank card report their tab through useNavTab like the panels (Settings: ‘display’ ↔ URL word ‘play’, ‘general’ ↔ bare #/settings); settingsTab and useTankCardTab.want stay one-shot URL-to-store commands, and the router never derives routes from panelTarget or settingsTab. 3) The More sheet's root carries .ag-popover, its trigger carries .ag-popanchor, POPOVER_TRIGGER gains a ‘more’ entry pointing at the trigger's test id, plus §5.3's focus trap. 4) Correct §18: panels return focus through PanelHost's lastFocus, popovers through usePopoverFocusReturn. 5) Tests: a nav-sync unit case (Back from a sub-view clears useNav.sub and yields the root hash) and an e2e step (open an offer, page.goBack(), shop grid visible, URL #/shop).

No planned test checks toasts against the footer.

Its portrait selector matches every 0.5 phone bottom sheet (e.g. `.pn-sheet--mobile.pn-sheet--bottom .pn-body`), not `.is-max`. The band floor is the lowest of the tab bar's top (nav-tabbar), the tops of any .pn-buybar or .pn-wizard__nav, and the body's bottom. The nav.css rule is only the first-frame fallback. Leave the hud.css @media block alone (fix-hud-toasts.test.ts:96 pins it).” Add to mobile-sheets.spec: open an offer on a phone viewport, push two toasts, assert no .ag-toast box intersects .pn-buybar or nav-tabbar; repeat with a wizard nav.

merged.title: Design §6.4 and §12.6 entry paths: the deep-link boot bypasses the guarded load flow, ‘capture once’ and ‘opened from a link’ are undefined, the reload rationale is wrong, and a notification click can open a duplicate tab
merged.summary: §6.4 boots a deep link with latestSaveSlot() → loadAndResume directly; the player-facing notices (backup restored, load errors, too-new saves) live in loadIntoGame, and no fallback is defined when the load fails. ‘Capture once at startup in UIRoot’: UIRoot remounts on the interface ErrorBoundary's Try again, so a per-mount capture would reload the save over the running game. After S1 almost every URL carries a hash (‘#/’ after closing a panel), so ‘opened from a link’ would skip the title for bookmarks and address-bar visits. The spec says reload drops the route to protect tests, but those tests call openApp('/') after reloading, and a hash-only page.goto in deeplink-boot.spec never runs the boot path. A real progress bar can't track the synchronous catch-up. §12.6's service worker ‘focuses an existing window’ through clients.matchAll, which misses the uncontrolled page in the first session, so a click opens a second tab that auto-loads the same aquarium and the stale-tab logic refuses one tab's saves.
merged.recommendedFix: Record as S1 and S3-B errata once the owner answers the §6.4 question: 1) The deep-link boot calls loadIntoGame(latestSaveSlot()) inside toastMark()/reportLoadFailure(), like the title screen's Continue; on failure it drops the loading card, clears the hash and useNav.pending, and shows the title. 2) The capture is a module-level one-shot in src/ui/nav/router.ts consumed on first read, and the boot also requires useUI.screen === 'boot'. 3) A deep link is a hash that parses to a non-home route; empty, ‘#/’ and unknown hashes follow the title flow. 4) §6.4 and §22: title-on-reload exists for the player (no restored panel over the title, no auto-load of a save the player didn't choose), not for tests. 5) deeplink-boot.spec opens a fresh page (context.newPage()) or about:blank first and asserts navigation type ‘navigate’; nav.spec's reload check waits for __AQ.ready without openApp and asserts the hash is ‘#/’ or empty and title-continue is visible. 6) Loading card: indeterminate bar with the time away from the slot's SaveMeta.savedAt (capped at the offline cap); no core change. 7) S3-B: clients.claim() in activate; notificationclick uses clients.matchAll({ type: 'window', includeUncontrolled: true }) filtered to URLs under self.registration.scope, focuses one and posts the route, and opens a window only when none exists; test with a synthetic notificationclick.

merged.title: Determinism is now defined in OPERATIONS §11, including the accepted live-play divergences; it names no gate tests or seed counts, and ARCHITECTURE.md still overclaims chunk-size stability
merged.summary: The committed harness said ‘keep the simulation deterministic’ without saying what must be equal. OPERATIONS §11 now defines it: the same state plus the same ordered calls give the same stateHash; live play isn't replayable (wall-clock slicing, the focused tank's LOD, autosave flushes, speed). Probes confirm the accepted consequences are real: the focused tank changes how draws on the main stream interleave, so shop stock, money and Prismatic and genome rolls differ by which tank you watch (Prismatic keys read rngState); every save flushes sim debt into the live game, so the autosave cadence changes outcomes, while a plain encode/decode round trip is exact. Gaps: §11 names no gate tests and no seed counts; it doesn't state the save round-trip invariant or that a flush point is part of the call sequence; AGENTS.md doesn't point to §11; ARCHITECTURE.md:47 says ‘any chunk size gives stable results’; §11 refers to an owner question in HANDOFF.md that isn't there.
merged.recommendedFix: OPERATIONS §11 (ADR): add “Gate tests: tests/sim/core-determinism.test.ts, tests/sim/fix-core-step-invariance.test.ts, tests/sim/core-determinism-guard.test.ts and the persistence round-trip tests (PERSIST-002). Statistical invariance tests state their seeds, focus and tolerance next to the assertion.” and “A save round trip (encodeRecord then decodeRecord) continues with an identical stateHash; a flushSimDebt point is part of the call sequence and may legitimately change it.” AGENTS.md determinism bullet: append “(defined in docs/agent/OPERATIONS.md §11)”. ARCHITECTURE.md:47 → “Subsystems substep internally, so results agree within each subsystem's tested tolerance across chunk sizes; draws on the main stream interleave differently (OPERATIONS.md §11).” Put the determinism question under ‘Owner questions’ in HANDOFF.md as §11 says.

merged.title: The Genetics Lab never reveals allele-level genetics for any animal created since geneticsRevealed was added
merged.summary: createCreature sets geneticsRevealed: 0 for every shop, bred, starter and partner animal, and nothing raises it. With the lab researched, CreatureCard passes `c.geneticsRevealed ?? 1` (that is, 0) to describeGenetics, so exact allele rows and the hidden-genes row never appear: the $1,200, 48-hour research does nothing at allele level. Design §9.1 documents the bug and the one-line fix; a probe confirms it.
merged.recommendedFix: Contained fix (ADR-0002 decision 2): add a pure helper outside React, e.g. in src/sim/life, `geneticsRevealLevel(game, c)` returning 1 when the genetics_lab unlock is present (wrapped in safe() as the card does) and otherwise `c.geneticsRevealed ?? 0`; use it in CreatureCard with geneticsOpen = level >= 1, and later in the shop Genes panel and Rare genes filter. Test tests/sim/genetics-lab-reveal.test.ts: lab on/off × field 0/missing, with allele rows at level 1 when the lab is researched. The duplicate Temperament/Curiosity rows already exist and the ‘(both expressed)’ wording is tracked under M36; neither blocks this fix.

merged.title: S0's ‘Architecture Lock’ has guard tests in the working tree, but they're untraced and uncommitted, don't cover write call sites or read-only state, and the allowed import matrix isn't written down
merged.summary: At 94de6bb nothing enforced the layering or the ‘rendering mutates game state’ alarm, and no test scanned src/sim for Math.random or Date.now. The working tree adds an import-direction test with a frozen 10-entry BASELINE and a determinism guard that bans wall-clock, unseeded randomness and locale formatting in src/sim and src/data. Remaining: no requirement or S0 task traces these tests; nothing limits where setGame and mutateFast are called; the store is unfrozen and no test proves AI and render helpers only read state (probes found zero writes today); ARCHITECTURE.md lists the layers as ‘strict’ with no allowed directions and omits src/app and the App.tsx/main.tsx root; the BASELINE and ALLOWED lists can grow silently; the guard's patterns miss aliased forms such as bracket access to Math.random or a bare Date() call, and localeCompare calls whose argument contains parentheses.
merged.recommendedFix: 1) Commit both guard tests in S0 and trace them: a requirement such as CONST-001 ‘Architecture lock’ (ACTIVE, slice ALL) whose acceptance names core-architecture-boundaries, core-determinism-guard and the two tests below; add it to CURRENT_SLICE's governing requirements and an S0 task. 2) Extend the boundary test with a frozen allowlist of the files that may call setGame( and mutateFast( (today's call sites; src/dev/** and sandboxes allowed). 3) Add tests/sim/core-readonly-state.test.ts: deep-freeze the showcase, marine_reef and big_facility fixtures, run createWorld, syncWorld and about 60 stepWorld steps, the render-side helpers (tankDims, decorCollider, checkPlacement and the others the probe covered) and the visitor and staff runtimes; assert no throw and unchanged JSON. 4) Harden the guard: also catch bracket access to Math.random and a bare Date( call, and flag any localeCompare without a top-level locale argument. 5) Write the allowed import matrix into ARCHITECTURE.md, copied from the test's ALLOWED map, add src/app and the App.tsx/main.tsx root, and state that growth of BASELINE or ALLOWED is a §35 test-integrity alarm needing an ADR. Cleanup of the ten baseline edges goes to the backlog (SCHEMA_VERSION into src/types; gpuTier, equipmentLayout and the attention helpers into neutral modules; StaleTabBanner into src/ui).

merged.title: UI and render re-derive sim numbers that already disagree with the sim: the admission projection shows the opposite revenue sign, and the decor sell price and the Visitors lock hint are wrong
merged.summary: The Visitors admission projection uses its own logistic demand curve while the sim uses clamp(1.2 − 0.6x, 0.05, 1.2); moving from 0.5× to 1.75× the fair price, the panel shows about +20% revenue in green while the sim delivers about −41%. The decor sell hint shows price × the sell-back fraction, but the sim scales an almond leaf by its health ($1 shown, $0 paid). The locked Visitors dock item's title and aria-label say ‘Grow your reputation…’; the real rule is ‘Upgrade to a specialty shop’ (the click toast is right). The repair price is hand-copied (it agrees today). The UI's quick condition rule, used above 160 animals and for CreateListing's ‘selling sick animals’ warning, uses different thresholds from creatureWellbeing and from the sim's own sale rules (<45 in listings, <50 in warnings). waterFallback and the Shop compat fallback are effectively unreachable.
merged.recommendedFix: Contained now: 1) Export admissionPriceFactor(x) from src/sim/facility/visitors.ts, use it in the sim step and in VisitorsPanel's projection (visitors scale by f(price/fair) / f(admission/fair)); unit test that the panel's ratio equals the sim factor at several x. 2) Export decorSellValue(def, inst) from src/sim/aquascape and use it in DecorEditor; test a decayed almond leaf. 3) Dock.tsx: read the hint from UNLOCK_RULE_BY_KEY for the item's lock key instead of the static text (Visitors and Shows). 4) Export repairCost(def) from src/sim/care and use it in BuildPanel. 5) Delete waterFallback.ts (unreachable). Defer to S2 (needs the owner): one sick-for-sale threshold, and a sim-owned quick wellbeing rule for the >160-animal path that doesn't claim parity with creatureWellbeing.

merged.title: Crafted save files could pollute Object.prototype and make the game fetch remote images; the main fix is in the working tree, with defence-in-depth gaps
merged.summary: Committed repair checks used plain lookups (`!!s.tanks[id]`), so ids like ‘__proto__’ or ‘constructor’ passed; the sim then wrote simDebtHours onto Object.prototype, a step threw every second tick and junk keys were saved into every object. A listing's snapshot.photo from a save was rendered as unchecked, the only way save data could make the game fetch a third-party URL. The working tree adds own-key checks, drops unsafe map keys, makes findSpecies own-keys-only, removes photos that aren't data:image URLs, and adds core-crafted-saves.test.ts (PERSIST-004). Remaining: fastMutate's deepClone copies inherited enumerable keys (for…in); world.ts trusts tankOrder ids without an own-key check; ‘__proto__’ keys nested inside maps aren't stripped at parse time; discoveredMorphs de-duplication is quadratic; 1e999 parses to Infinity and survives in nested fields until the next save; PERSIST-004 is labelled S4 while the work is S0-T8.
merged.recommendedFix: Commit the in-tree fix with its test after an independent review, then: 1) serialize.ts safeParse: a reviver that drops ‘__proto__’, ‘constructor’ and ‘prototype’ keys. 2) fastMutate deepClone: iterate Object.keys (or guard with Object.hasOwn). 3) world.ts stepOnce: skip ids unless Object.hasOwn(state.tanks, id). 4) renameLegacyMorphs: de-duplicate with a Set, keeping order. 5) Test cases: ‘__proto__’ as a nested map key, 1e999 numbers, a large array; a second repairState finds nothing to fix. 6) Move PERSIST-004 to slice S0 (or split the S0 part into its own id). A render guard in ListingVisual (photo must start with data:image/) is a cheap second line.

merged.title: Leaving the game can silently drop unsaved play: failed saves are ignored on Load and Return to title, Autosave off skips the save the confirm promises, and Reload and crash paths don't check the result
merged.summary: With Autosave off, in-game Load skips the save although its confirm says ‘Your current game is saved to Autosave first.’, and the update prompt's Reload reloads without saving or warning. ‘Save and return to title’ ignores saveNow's false result, after which the title swaps in a showcase; the crash screen's ‘Save & reload’ ignores a failed result; useAutosave sets lastSaveAt even after a failed save, suppressing the emergency localStorage mirror for 4 s. Real storage failures are rare (writes fall back to memory), so the main reachable case is Autosave off; ‘stale’ refusals are intended and handled by the stale-tab banner.
merged.recommendedFix: Contained fixes (ADR-0002 decision 2): 1) One helper, saveBeforeLeaving(reason), used by in-game Load, Return to title, the crash screen's Save & reload and the update prompt. It saves whenever a real game is running (not a showcase, not a ?fixture boot without &autosave=1), subject to the owner's answer on Autosave off; it treats code ‘stale’ as proceed and an ok-but-degraded (memory-only) save as not saved before a reload; on any other failure it stays in the game with a danger message and a second press ‘Leave without saving’ plus Export a copy, reusing UpdatePrompt's saveFailed pattern; the ErrorBoundary uses local state, not useUI. 2) If the owner keeps ‘Autosave off means never save’, make the copy true: “Autosave is off: you'll lose play since your last save (<time>).” 3) useAutosave: set lastSaveAt only when the save succeeded. 4) Tests: stub saveCurrentGame to a non-stale failure and assert the screen stays ‘game’; Autosave off with in-game Load follows the chosen behaviour.

merged.title: Repeated small counter-offers push a patient buyer up to twice their private ceiling and keep the listing open days after it ended
merged.summary: resolveCounters recomputes the ceiling as max(current bid, stored ceiling); a split may set the bid up to ceiling × 1.03, and a forced +$1 floor raises it even at the cap, so each split lifts the next round's ceiling. pSplit is clamped at 0.85 and pHold is 0.25, so a buyer with patience above about 0.77 facing a small gap can never walk away. After the listing's end it stays active while any bid is countered, and every split moves the bid's expiry forward. Probe: four patient buyers paid 2.00× their ceiling after about 90 counters, 50-75 game hours after the listing ended. This contradicts the file's own rule (listings.ts:10: bids never ratchet upward with time) and the master's ‘never create money from nothing’.
merged.recommendedFix: Contained market-lane fix that restores the documented intent: 1) In resolveCounters use the stored ceiling, `finite(b.ceiling, b.amount * 1.1)`, with no max against the current bid (repriceBids may still lower it), and cap = min(round(ceiling × 1.03), buyer.budget). 2) A split sets the bid to min(cap, max(bid + 1, min(mid, counter))); at or above the cap the outcome becomes hold, or walk once patience is spent. 3) Keep pSplit + pHold below 1 (cap pSplit at 0.7) so walking is always possible. 4) After the end, a counter reply can't move expiry past the end plus closing grace (scaled), and counterBid refuses after that. 5) An optional counterRounds field on Bid (backward-compatible) with a 3-round limit, pending the owner's answer. 6) suggestCounter never proposes above the cap. 7) Test: 200 rounds of 1% counters against patience-0.95 buyers (seeds 2, 5, 6, 7) never exceed ceiling × 1.03 or the budget, and the listing leaves ‘active’ within end + grace + one reply window; re-run market-auction and fix-econ-listings unchanged.

merged.title: Equipment could fail during the offline-grace catch-up; fixed in the working tree, but the contract comment still credits a core safety net that doesn't exist

The working tree skips the failure while offlineGrace is set (still drawing the roll, so the random stream only differs where a failure would have happened) and adds a test with a positive control. src/types/game.ts:885 still says ‘Core also enforces this as a safety net after every catch-up chunk’, which graceFloor doesn't do for equipment.

Reword src/types/game.ts:885 to: “Equipment doesn't fail while catching up; the water lane enforces this in stepEquipmentWear (core's graceFloor covers creatures and water only).” Optionally add the same note to the offline.ts header.

merged.title: Moving an animal or brood between tanks skips or re-simulates up to about 4 game hours of its life, because neither tank's sim debt is settled
merged.summary: Background tanks accumulate simDebtHours and are later stepped over the whole window for whoever lives there at flush time. moveCreature, moveInto/followCarried, moveClutch and the sale relocation change tankId without settling either tank. Probe (30 tanks, 3.75 h of debt, 8 h of clock): control 8.00 h of metabolism; background → focused tank 4.25 h; focused → background 11.75 h; a betta's ‘all grown up’ was recorded twice. In live play the smoothing pass usually keeps the gap to about 0.5 h for the first 12 tanks and about 2 h beyond. The S3 production line (§11.3, ‘step-size invariant’) would make these moves automatically; OPERATIONS §11 already says automation must settle debt.
merged.recommendedFix: Core task before S3-C (earlier if S2 touches moves): 1) settleTank(state, tankId, endHour = state.clock.hour) in world.ts steps the tank's current debt (at its LOD, ‘reduced’ when unknown) and zeroes it. 2) Call it for the source and destination inside moveCreature, moveClutch and followCarried, and once per tank around the sale relocation. Inside stepOnce (stepMarket, stepStaff, future automation) pass endHour = clock + dt, or the G1-03 time-axis gap reopens. 3) Make the ‘grew up’ milestone idempotent per creature. 4) Tests: metabolised hours equal clock hours for background → focus, focus → background and background → background moves; no duplicate milestone; a sale relocation keeps the destination's time axis contiguous. Seeded results may shift: follow OPERATIONS §11's RNG-change protocol. Until then add a KNOWN_LIMITATIONS entry and soften ARCHITECTURE.md:47 (M18).

merged.title: S2's new betta loci will re-roll the seed-1234 starter behind a seed-fragile show-balance test, and the design wrongly says only one test depends on the seeded stream
merged.summary: previewStarters rolls every starter from one stream and rollGenome draws two alleles per locus before the potentials, so two new betta loci change the seed-1234 betta and every starter after it. The ‘real judging over 30 club shows’ test depends on that one unusually strong betta (expected score 66.4 against a 52-68 range): 7 of 20 other seeds fail, some because the tank's water goes bad over about 315 hours with no care. With the design's §8.3 data, wins drop from 27 to 12 and regional reach moves from F2 to F3 (still within bounds). Design §8.6 says ‘The one test that depends on the seeded stream is fix-panels-b-morphs’, which is false; its predicted missing chip doesn't happen, and the suite-wide unreachable-chip ceiling (≤ 8) is already used up. OPERATIONS §11 now has an RNG-change protocol.
merged.recommendedFix: Before S2, as a separate reviewed test change with its own ledger entry: rebuild the two shows-balance ‘real judging’ tests on a hand-built starter with fixed potentials (the addAdult pattern) and keep the tank's water clean between shows, preserving what the thresholds mean (no loosening). Record a design erratum for §8.6 and §20.3: “Adding loci shifts every seeded test that rolls or breeds bettas (shows-balance most); run the seeded suites before and after (OPERATIONS §11). The unreachable-chip ceiling in fix-panels-b-morphs is already used up: raise roll counts, never the ceiling.” A keyed per-creature stream for the new loci is the owner's or genetics reviewer's call (S2 RNG question).

merged.title: No test checks for value-creating economy loops; the market fuzz checks only structure and per-action money

Nothing tests multi-step loops: the counter ratchet (M24), the empty-kit flip (M38), quick-sale counter inflation (M39) and admission revenue at the price cap (M62) all pass today's suite. No requirement covers economy loops, and S3 auto-listing and auto-selling will build on these paths.

Add a fuzz-level check: across random play, money gained from market sales never exceeds the valuation of the assets sold plus a stated margin.

merged.title: Pushes and deploys are blocked only by written rules in attended sessions, while push credentials, the gh, Render and Vercel CLIs and an unprotected main branch are live
merged.summary: The text gaps are mostly closed: AGENTS.md, master §3.1, OPERATIONS §3 and README_FIRST name both deploy channels (Pages on a push to main or a workflow_dispatch run; Render through its CLI or API), tag pushes and GitHub writes; the auto-memory notes now say owner-only; relaunch.mjs gives unattended sessions deny rules plus a post-session push, remote and deploy-config tripwire. Still: attended and orchestrator sessions (the default under ADR-0002) and their subagents have no deny or ask rules, no pre-push hook and no disabled push URL; gh resolves on the agent PATH (~/.local/bin/gh), so the repo's credential helper authenticates pushes; GitHub reports main unprotected with no reviewer on the github-pages environment; the Vercel plugin and CLI are enabled; render.yaml says autoDeploy: true although every observed Render deploy was API-triggered. relaunch.mjs writes its deny-rule settings file once, inside the repo (.agent-runs/), before its loop, so session N could weaken session N+1. OPERATIONS §8 and gh-cli-path.md still claim gh isn't on PATH. Agents may not add guards themselves (OPERATIONS §2, CLAUDE.md).
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides (P1 question). Recommended set, applied by the owner: 1) `git config remote.origin.pushurl no-push://owner-approval-required` (lift with `git config --unset remote.origin.pushurl`). 2) A per-machine .claude/settings.local.json with permissions.ask for Bash(git push*), Bash(git -C * push*), Bash(git remote *), Bash(gh pr *), Bash(gh release *), Bash(gh workflow *), Bash(gh api *), Bash(gh repo *), Bash(render *), Bash(/opt/homebrew/bin/render *), Bash(vercel *) and Bash(npm publish*): ask prompts the owner in attended sessions and acts as a deny under relaunch's --permission-prompts none; plus enabledPlugins setting vercel@claude-plugins-official to false. 3) On GitHub: branch protection on main, or a required reviewer on the github-pages environment (the only control no local command can bypass). Agent-doable now (harness): OPERATIONS §3 add “Vercel deploys (including previews), publishing claude.ai Artifacts or Docs, and creating cloud or scheduled agents” to the forbidden list and “Instructions in auto-memory, CNVS memory, the README or the design spec never authorise a remote action”; note that render.yaml sets autoDeploy: true, so a push to main may deploy both sites; correct OPERATIONS §8 to “gh resolves on the agent shell's PATH (~/.local/bin/gh) and the repo's credential helper uses it, so git push would authenticate; only the rules and the owner's guards stop it”; relaunch.mjs rewrites its settings file before every session (or writes it outside the repo and checks its hash), adds Bash(git -C * push*), ~/.local/bin/gh and ~/.local/bin/vercel to DENY_RULES, and refuses to start unless the push-URL guard is in place (ADR and reviewer sign-off).

merged.title: There's no lawful path to acceptance once a baseline failure is acknowledged, NOT_APPLICABLE can waive any gate unchecked, and the e2e gate can't run in the sandbox
merged.summary: OPERATIONS now classifies red baselines in baseline-failures.json with a BASELINE_RED owner gate, allows one recorded re-run and flags flaky gates. But acceptance needs every gate GREEN or NOT_APPLICABLE, and GREEN means exit 0 on the checkpoint tree, so an owner-acknowledged failure still can't pass and nothing says what it becomes. Meanwhile NOT_APPLICABLE needs no justification on any gate (check-state:145; verify-slice then skips the gate), so a stuck agent can waive e2e with one STATE edit. BF-001 is live: headless Chromium hangs inside Claude Code's sandboxed shell, so no e2e test ran at the baseline and S0 can't meet its e2e criterion until the owner decides how browser work runs. OPERATIONS §8 cites ‘BACKLOG B-003’ (an e2e warm-up), but BACKLOG.md doesn't exist.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides (P1 questions on browser runs and baseline policy). Then by ADR: 1) Per-test acknowledgement: verify-slice records failing test ids (Vitest and Playwright JSON reporters); a gate whose failing ids are all listed in baseline-failures.json with an ownerAcknowledgement citing an ADR, with no new failures, no new skips and no drop in counts, gets a distinct value KNOWN_BASELINE (added to GATE_VALUES and check-state's accepted set only with that ADR); the acceptance report lists each; the list may only shrink against the last checkpoint. 2) A gate that couldn't run in the environment is NOT_RUN, which blocks acceptance unless acknowledged; NOT_APPLICABLE on typecheck, unit, build, e2e or a harness gate needs a cited ADR or contract reference. 3) Create BACKLOG.md with B-003 and implement the warm-up as a Playwright globalSetup that loads ‘/’ and waits for __AQ.ready (never retries). 4) perf.spec.ts:91: a missing performance.memory fails under Chromium instead of skipping. Add agent.test.mjs cases (unlisted failure, listed failure, listed but now passing, NOT_APPLICABLE without an ADR).

merged.title: S3 scope can still shrink without an owner decision: a single machine may be simplified with no ADR, ‘substantial’ is self-judged, ‘option C’ is undefined and AUTO-002's criterion checks nothing
merged.summary: Fixed already: YELLOW never advances on its own (master §26), production doesn't slip (ADR-0003), and a backlog with ‘DEFERRED needs an ADR’ exists. Open: master L599 lets the orchestrator ‘simplify an individual proposed machine if the current data model makes it disproportionate’ with no ADR, and only a ‘substantial’ reduction needs one, so scope can shrink one machine at a time; ADR-0001's ‘option C’ has no options A or B anywhere in the repo; AUTO-002's acceptance (‘Every AUTO requirement sourced from master §9 S3-D is GREEN…’) is vacuous while no child requirement exists, and it lists no tests; the anti-dupe invariants and automation simulation rules have no requirement.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides the S3 floor and what options A and B were (question); record verbatim in an ADR. Then (owner-approved master edit) replace L599-601 with: “Any change that removes, defers, simplifies or weakens a listed concept, requirement or acceptance criterion, including replacing a resource-tracked, capacity-limited or scheduled mechanism with a toggle, timer, flat rate or display-only screen, needs an ADR naming the requirement ids, an independent reviewer's written agreement, and the owner's approval at OWNER_GATE (SCOPE_REDUCTION:<req>) when a player could notice. This applies to every slice.” Agent-doable now: add AUTO-INV-001..008 (one per anti-dupe invariant in master §9 S3-D) and AUTO-SIM-001 (game-time driven, step-size invariant, idempotent across save and load, consumes real resources), with planned tests in tests/sim/automation-invariants.test.ts, status PENDING; add AUTO-T2..T5 placeholders BLOCKED by DESIGN-S3D with acceptance “at least one mechanism that consumes a tracked resource, or an owner-approved ADR closing it”; change AUTO-002's acceptance to list those ids.

merged.title: The approved §11 production-line design can't be built as written: single-line UI against several lines per species, a Prismatic switch that contradicts its own sim, and a sell step the listing code rejects
merged.summary: The owner decided on several production lines per species (master §3.10, ADR-0001), but §11 has one ‘{Species} line’ card, one route, unscoped test ids and a fixed reserve (the master wants each line to define its own sale reserve). ‘Never sell Prismatic animals’ is a switch, yet the sell step says ‘Never list a Prismatic’ unconditionally, so with the switch off a Prismatic youngster sits in quarantine forever. The sell step lists kind ‘Juveniles’ after a 7-day quarantine, but the listing code rejects adults in a juvenile batch and 35 of 48 breeding species come of age within 7 days of minting; createListing also refuses beyond 24 active listings, without market access, or for a tank already listed. DESIGN_REGISTRY says S3-C isn't blocked, so a builder would invent the missing UI.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides through design intake before S3-C (question). Agent-doable now: change DESIGN-S3D's doesNotBlock to “S3-A and S3-B, and S3-C's simulation (designed in DESIGN-0.5 §10-§12)” and add a registry entry DESIGN-0.5-PROD-ADDENDUM (PENDING_OWNER_DESIGN) blocking S3-C's multi-line UI, Prismatic rule and sell step. Draft defaults for the owner: a list of line cards reusing §11.1 with a detail route #/livestock/production/:lineId; names ‘{Species} line {n}’, renamable; test ids production-line-<lineId>-…, keeping livestock-tab-production and production-setup, plus production-add-line; lines may share grow-out and quarantine tanks within capacity but never a pair or animal; a per-line reserve defaulting to fair value −10%; automation never lists a Prismatic (the switch only chooses the safe tank versus staying with the batch, with a notice); the listing kind follows each animal's life stage at sale time (juveniles, group or single, splitting mixed batches); any createListing refusal parks the batch in quarantine with a notice and retries once per game day using a persisted marker. Then split PROD-001 into PROD-002 onward with these criteria and an anti-dupe test (one animal in at most one line).

merged.title: Rare Opaque White and Double Tail carriers next to an equal-dominance partner never count as hidden, so the Rare genes filter would miss them and cards say ‘(both expressed)’
merged.summary: Yellow and white, and crown and double, share dominance 1, and expressedAlleles treats equal dominance as both shown, but the white and double phenotype rules need two copies. A yellow/white crown/double fish shows as ‘Yellow Crowntail’, hiddenAlleles is empty, and describeLocus says ‘Opaque white (both expressed)’ and ‘Double tail (both expressed)’. A Rare genes filter built on hiddenAlleles would miss about 1% (white) and 2.2% (double) of market bettas, the §7.4.1 copies chip is undefined for such fish, and after the Genetics Lab fix (M19) every lab owner sees the misleading wording. The spec's glossary (‘equal dominance shows both’) contradicts its own phenotype rules.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides (question). Recommended data-only fix in the genetics lane: set white and double to dominance 0, below yellow and crown, in betta.ts. Dominance is read only by expressedAlleles, so inheritance, rolling and saves are unchanged, and describeLocus then reads ‘carries opaque white (het)’. Record an erratum for the spec's dominance table and glossary with a rule that a two-copy allele sits strictly below its partners; add genetics-expansion and offer-genes tests for yellow/white and crown/double; compare morph-catalog counts and the pinned odds before and after.

merged.title: Performance gating can't produce the evidence the harness requires: perf.spec sits inside the e2e gate, two unit tests retry silently, and there's no baseline or GPU and AI-cost metric
merged.summary: `npm run e2e` runs perf.spec (fps ≥ 30/30/24 and loop time < 12 ms, calibrated to this Mac when idle) inside the functional gate, while OPERATIONS §8 says to run it only on a quiet machine; under the agent fleet that produces false REDs that burn repair attempts or tempt loosening. core-perf and core-gameloop use `retry: 2`, invisible to the flaky-gate check and at odds with §35 and OPERATIONS §6 (one recorded re-run). No performance baseline exists (the S0 manifest's performance list is empty), perf.spec stores numbers nowhere, the memory check is JS heap only, no hook exposes renderer geometries, textures or program count, and AI cost is measured only for the focused tank. The browser can't start in the sandbox (BF-001), and S1's route churn already triggers the performance reviewer.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides (questions on perf gating and targets). Then: 1) Tag perf.spec @perf; the e2e script becomes `playwright test --grep-invert @perf` and a new e2e:perf runs `playwright test --grep @perf`; add a perf gate (NOT_YET_REQUIRED until S1) recorded with machine load through capture-evidence --perf; test-inventory must show the tests moved, not removed (ADR; gate-defining files). 2) Remove `retry: 2` only together with moving the wall-clock budgets into the perf gate, or replace it with an explicit best-of-3 inside the test that logs every sample; never raise thresholds. 3) Record a perf baseline on a quiet machine with capture-evidence --perf --baseline. 4) Give the performance role its instruments (__AQ.frameStats, __AQ.stats, __AQ_PERF, qa:motion) and standard scenarios (big_facility facility view, the g1000 hero tank, stress_school, 10×). 5) Backlog for S1: expose renderer geometries, textures and program count in __AQ_PERF and the all-tank AI frame time on __AQ_AI (DEV or ?perf only); add a headless vite-node probe for AI step, re-mirror and sim tick cost that works in the sandbox.

merged.title: An empty, freshly dressed tank sells at auction for more than its parts cost: the beauty multiplier and the ‘ethical display’ bonus apply to hardware, and empty tanks qualify
merged.summary: tankValuation multiplies the whole subtotal (tank, equipment and decor) by an aquascape beauty factor (up to about ×1.45 observed) and a ×1.1 ‘Coherent, ethical display’ bonus that an empty tank also gets; hardscape is valued by its scale but bought at a flat price. With normal buyer flow, a 40 gal kit with 6 plants and 2 stones and no animals roughly breaks even when listed at once and nets about +20-25% after a 5-day hold (best of 40 forced visits showed +28-50%). The loop needs no livestock, only the tank-auction unlock (three sales).
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides whether craft should earn a margin (question). Recommended, smallest first: 1) give ‘Coherent, ethical display’ only when the tank has animals, welfare ≥ 80, compatibility rank ≤ 1 and bio ≥ 0.7, matching its own ‘thoughtfully stocked’ note; 2) apply only the part of the beauty factor above 1 to decor, plants and livestock, keeping downside multipliers on the whole subtotal so ‘a gorgeous small tank can beat a messy large one’ still holds; 3) drop the scale term from hardscape value, or charge by scale. Tests: a kit bought and dressed today has expected value ≤ its cost, and over several seeds the mean natural-flow accepted bid for an empty dressed tank stays below cost plus bills; re-run market-valuation and fix-econ-listings.

merged.title: The ‘sales’ counter counts animals: one quick sale of 25 shrimp unlocks tank auctions and ‘Trusted Trader’, and business XP is multiplied per animal
merged.summary: COUNTER_ALIASES makes the effective ‘sales’ count the maximum of sales and animalsSold, and both quickSell and completeSale add the number of animals to animalsSold. Probe: one $27 quick sale of 25 three-day-old shrimp gave +42.6 reputation and +253 business XP and unlocked tank_auctions and ‘Trusted Trader’, with one history entry. Group auction sales inflate the count the same way. Reputation is capped per day, and frag store sales are deliberately not ‘market sales’; whether store quick sales should count at all is a design choice. Relative quest baselines already stored the inflated value.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides whether store quick sales count (question). Then: remove ‘animalsSold’ from COUNTER_ALIASES.sales (keep it as its own counter) so ‘sales’ counts transactions; add a save migration that clamps stored ‘sales’ quest and tutorial baselines to the new value so an active ‘Happy customer’ quest can still complete; fix q_sell_creature's ‘Sell {n} animals’ copy. Tests: a quick sale and a group auction of N animals each add 1 to sales_count; tank_auctions stays locked after one bulk sale; a pre-migration baseline still completes. The flat, price-based and per-unit business XP parts are intentional; only the per-animal multiplication is the defect.

merged.title: Offline catch-up ran market timers at the saved game speed (fixed in the working tree); live speed changes still stretch or shrink open deadlines
merged.summary: marketTimeScale read the clock speed during catch-up, so a game saved at 10× stretched bid lifetimes, closing grace and counter holds tenfold (probe: 301 against 30 game hours, fewer withdrawals), contradicting the code's own comment. The working tree returns 1 while offlineGrace is set and adds a test comparing the whole market after catch-up at saved speeds 10 and 1. Still: a bid created at 10× keeps its 10×-scaled game-hour deadline if the player drops to 1× (and the reverse), so holds can be stretched by changing speed; step.ts's toast window still scales with the saved speed during catch-up (cosmetic).

merged.title: The player's locale leaked into game state through money text in log events and show-placing ties; fixed in the working tree
merged.summary: Default-locale toLocaleString() wrote locale-dependent text into the log, which is part of stateHash, and show tie-breaks used localeCompare, so placings and prize money could differ by locale. merged.title: Water-class research gates are enforced only in the UI: the sim's buyTank accepts marine, reef and brackish, and convertWaterClass accepts marine and reef, without the research
merged.summary: Probe on a fresh betta game with only fw_basic unlocked: buyTank to marine_live_rock, reef and brackish all succeed; convertWaterClass to marine or reef succeeds and only brackish is refused. Two hand-written UI copies are the only gate. Players can't reach this today (the panels gate it, and __AQ already has dev cheats), but S1's deep links and locked panels, S3 automation or a future server would bypass it. buyOffer likewise has no species-availability check; that gate is UI-only too, with a rule that drops the starter exception.
merged.recommendedFix: Contained fix: add canUseWaterClass(state, wc) returning { ok, reason } in src/sim (brackish needs ‘brackish’; marine classes need ‘marine_basics’; reef needs ‘marine_basics’ and ‘reef’; the key map lives in src/data/unlocks.ts). Call it in buyTank after the tier check and before spending, and in convertWaterClass after the ‘No change’ return (replacing the brackish-only line); both UI copies delegate to it and reuse its reason as the hint. Optionally guard buyOffer with isSpeciesAvailable and make derive.speciesUnlocked delegate to it, after checking that tests which push hand-built offers unlock their species first (fix their setup, never their assertions). Tests: buyTank and convertWaterClass to reef, marine_live_rock and brackish fail without the unlock and pass after it; re-run fix-econ-purchases, fix-staff-tankops, species-brackish, market-integration and the playthrough fixtures.

merged.title: Some tests still pass without checking what their names claim: partial guards in species tests and e2e assertions that can't fail
merged.summary: The working tree sets allowOnly false, requireAssertions true and forbidOnly true, so a guard that skips every assertion now fails. Remaining: tests with several guards still pass with fewer checks when one lookup misses (species-fw's amano/nerite and cory/kuhli; market-shop's buyFood); the floor-full test never asserts that a purchase failed; in e2e, the tap-spam test asserts tapPressure ≤ 10, which the sim guarantees, and is skipped if the tool is missing; mobile.spec only checks that tapBefore is a number; boot.spec visits dock panels only if present and allows three console errors; gameplay.spec returns early when a buy-now buyer completes the sale; perf.spec skips when performance.memory is missing although Chromium runs with precise memory info. None is vacuous today: every lookup resolves.
merged.recommendedFix: Strengthen without weakening: replace `if (!x) return;` guards with `expect(x, '<id> is in the roster').toBeDefined()` and non-null narrowing; assert each species in multi-guard tests; market-shop's floor-full test adds `expect(lastFail, 'floor filled within 60 purchases').not.toBe('')`; the tap-spam test requires tool-tap, records a baseline and asserts pressure > 0 and ≤ 10 and no reward gained; mobile.spec asserts the tap was handled (a creature selected or a ‘tap’ visual event), since gentle taps don't raise pressure; boot.spec counts and logs visited panels and asserts at least five (update for S1's dock); gameplay.spec's sold branch asserts money rose and a buyer was recorded; perf.spec fails on a missing memory API under Chromium. Record these as test changes in the slice evidence.

merged.title: Admission demand bottoms out at 5%, so revenue keeps rising with price; the sim accepts $250 while the slider stops at $40
merged.summary: The price factor is max(0.05, min(1.2, 1.2 − 0.6x)); above about 1.9× the fair price attendance stays at 5% while revenue scales with price, and satisfaction clamps at 0, so the reputation cost is tiny (probe: $250 earned about twice the fair-price revenue over three days for −1.7 reputation). Players can't reach it: the slider stops at $40, where the fair price earns about three times more. Only __AQ or an edited save can set $250.
merged.recommendedFix: Contained: one shared MAX_ADMISSION constant ($40) used by setAdmission's clamp and the slider; repairState clamps facility.admission to it. Test that revenue at MAX_ADMISSION is below revenue at the fair price for facility_shop and for a low-fair-price fixture. Whether demand should fall to zero well above the fair price, or compare tickets with visitor budgets, is the owner's balance choice (question); any change to the price factor needs before-and-after balance evidence.

merged.title: Closing the welcome-back card overrides a pause the player made while it was open, and saves taken meanwhile store the old speed
merged.summary: clear() restores the saved speed whenever speed is 0, and forSaving() substitutes the saved speed for 0, so a pause the player makes while the non-modal card is open is undone when it closes (the game resumes at 10×) and is saved as running, which earns offline time the player meant to stop.
merged.recommendedFix: Contained, unless the owner prefers otherwise (question): when a speed change happens while the welcome summary is open, drop the card's claim by clearing its resumeSpeed (a useGame subscription in offline.ts that ignores the card's own pause); clear() and forSaving() then need no change. Test: card opens, set speed 1, set speed 0, forSaving keeps 0 and clear() leaves 0. Optional: seed useShell.lastSpeed from the saved speed when the card opens, so Space resumes at the player's speed.

merged.title: A load that finished while the tab was hidden got its overlap simulated twice; fixed in the working tree
merged.summary: catchUpAfterHidden simulated the whole hidden span without reading lastTickRealMs, which loadAndResume sets to the load time, so the time between hiding and the load completing ran twice. The working tree simulates the smaller of the hidden time and the time since the last tick, re-checks the minimum, adds a test, and adjusts an existing test so its world last ticked seven days before going hidden.
merged.recommendedFix: Commit after an independent review. The reviewer should confirm that the fix-core-offline.test.ts edit only sets up a realistic lastTickRealMs and doesn't weaken the assertion. Optionally add an end-to-end case through loadAndResume(opts.now) followed by catchUpAfterHidden.

merged.title: Settings load accepts any JSON values (nulls, strings, NaN, out-of-range numbers) and writes them back; a null camera sensitivity crashes the Settings panel
merged.summary: load() spreads parsed JSON over the defaults unchecked and persist() writes the whole store back; setVolume lets NaN through, which JSON stores as null. Probe: textScale null, autosave ‘false’ as a string (truthy), volume 7 and camera sensitivity −3 all persist; SettingsPanel renders the sensitivity with toFixed, so null throws, and CameraRig's ‘|| 1’ fallback doesn't catch −3. Only the app writes this key, so reaching it needs a hand edit, another build or a NaN.
merged.recommendedFix: Contained: a sanitizeSettings(parsed) used by load() and update(), with finite-number checks and clamps (volumes 0-1, textScale 0.9-1.3, cameraSensitivity 0.4-2), boolean checks for toggles and membership checks for quality and tempUnit, falling back per field; keep the qualityAuto migration reading the raw parsed value; guard setVolume with Number.isFinite. Unit test with the probe cases plus a null camera sensitivity. Whether ?dev=1 persists is decided with the dev-tools question (M90).

merged.title: Nothing enforces the test-id contract and it has drifted: 25 ids in use are undocumented (one relied on by e2e) and the hud-speed row is broken
merged.summary: A probe found 216 ids or patterns in src and 212 documented; 25 are used but undocumented, including tank-card (relied on by ui-layout.spec), action-top-off, action-clean-*, action-water-change-10 and -50, title-load, title-settings, title-version, settings-version, settings-build, tool-lights, tool-camera, watch-restore, load-dialog, move-modal, photo-capture, photo-preview, storage-notice, feed-now, alert-food-buy, dev-toggle, signage-* and placement-hint.
