In test-inventory.mjs comments, call its entries ‘test names’.

merged.title: The compatibility cache is global, keyed on rounded values and shared with UI previews, so answers near thresholds can depend on history
merged.summary: Cache keys round size, bio-maturity and algae while the engine compares exact values against thresholds inside one rounding bucket; the cache clears completely at 256 entries and UI previews add entries, so when an entry is evicted depends on UI activity. world.ts records a past drift caused by this cache. Probes found no divergence today; S3 sorting that uses previewAddition or evaluateTank would inherit the risk.
merged.recommendedFix: Backlog for S3, before automation uses compatibility decisions: scope the sim's cache to a world step (clear it at the start of each advanceWorld slice, or key it on world identity plus sim time), give UI previews their own cache, or key the threshold-sensitive fields on exact values. Re-run staff-sim ‘is deterministic’ and core-determinism afterwards.

merged.title: RNG plumbing: coral nipping opens a second simRng inside a tank step and forks the main stream, and subsystem seeding and repair are ad hoc
merged.summary: stepTankPiece's ctx.rng and applyCoralNipping's own simRng(state) both start from the stored rngState, so the creature step replays the coral-nip draws and rewinds rngState (every piece, in a reef with a coral-nipper): nip outcomes and the next creature rolls are correlated, deterministically but with a bias. Subsystem streams are offsets in one mulberry32 cycle with ad-hoc seeds; repairState resets a bad shows.rng to the game seed, unlike ensureShowsState; newGame's comment ‘advance the RNG past the preview rolls’ describes a simple XOR. OPERATIONS §11 already says to use the step's ctx.rng inside a tank step.
merged.recommendedFix: Do it together with S2's RNG-stream change under §11's protocol, since both shift seeded results: 1) pass ctx.rng into stepTankDecor and applyCoralNipping as an optional trailing parameter (falling back to simRng(state)), or make simRng re-read state.rngState on every draw so every view shares one stream; 2) add streamSeed(seed, name) for new streams only (don't change the staff or shows seeds); 3) in repairState delete a non-finite shows.rng so ensureShowsState rebuilds it; 4) fix the newGame comment. Test: a reef with a coral-nipper, where rngState only advances and no ctx draw repeats a decor draw.

merged.title: Authoritative tank mutators (water conversion, substrate change, salt use) live in the UI lane, with a duplicated salt formula
merged.summary: convertWaterClass and changeSubstrate spend money, use up stored salt, reset chemistry and move gear and decor, all from src/ui. They run inside mutate, so the store boundary holds, but ARCHITECTURE.md says domain mutators live in src/sim and the salt-for-fill formula is copied outside the sim. This is a documented known limitation (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:82). The notify and photo-story writes are UI bookkeeping, not sim authority.
merged.recommendedFix: A no-behaviour-change refactor, before any S3-D water-preparation work or as the first task of the slice that needs it: move convertWaterClass and its cost, canChangeWaterClass, changeSubstrate and its cost, setBackdrop and the rename and purpose setters into src/sim/tanks/ops.ts with a re-export at the old path (tests unchanged); move the water-class and purpose label strings into src/data or return structured results; share saltKgFor(litres, fromSG, toSG) in src/sim/water/constants.ts while keeping each caller's rounding; drop the duplicate markLogRead; then remove KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:82.

merged.title: Species and food facts are hard-coded outside src/data: the ‘made for another animal’ rule exists four ways, and the sim branches on species ids and display names
merged.summary: Food ‘made for’ rules use id-prefix patterns in four places with different scoring; the ‘eats this food’ rule is re-implemented five times (ToolRail treats untagged food as edible); illness and compatibility branch on species ids and common names (a /shrimp/ name match decides whose young get eaten); seahorse snout reach is copied three times; PlacementGhost hard-codes the axolotl's water class. All agree today, but S2 catalog renames and S3 Tier 3 feed production would have to find every copy.
merged.recommendedFix: Schedule in S2 (catalog) and S3 Tier 3 (feed): add FoodDef.madeFor (species ids, behaviour sets, environments) and species fields (swim-bladder susceptibility; youngKind, set explicitly for peacock_mantis_shrimp); one isMadeForOther(species, food, environment) predicate while keeping each caller's weights; use eatsFood everywhere and decide ToolRail's unknown-food case on purpose; derive the default water class from the species' first water class; move seahorse reach into the render body-plan data. Pin today's outputs per species and food first so the move is provably behaviour-neutral. Add a guard rejecting species-id or common-name matching in src/sim and src/ui (allowlisting dev fixtures and the render and AI registries).

merged.title: There's no save-size budget, and the synchronous localStorage mirror fails silently above the browser's quota
merged.summary: saveGameSync returns false when localStorage throws, and autosave doesn't report it, although on reload and navigation the IndexedDB write may never land. The realistic worst case today is about 0.63 million characters plus 29 listing photos of up to 200,000 characters each; real browser quotas are unmeasured. S3's production lines and automation will make saves larger.
merged.recommendedFix: PERSIST-005 in S3: a maximum-scale fixture (most tanks, creatures and lines, 24 active and 5 closed listings with photos at the 200,000-character cap) and a unit test against a stated budget (e.g. 2 million characters, with a separate budget when localStorage is the main store); have saveGameSync drop listing photos when over budget so the emergency mirror always fits; log mirror failures to loopStats and warn once in the console, warning the player only if the IndexedDB save also fails.

merged.title: Source-text CSS tests pin text, not behaviour; S1's nav.css will override the pinned rules while those tests stay green
merged.summary: These tests read hud.css and other source files and regex-match exact blocks. The design tells S1 to override those blocks from a new nav.css instead of editing them, so the cascade can change (16 px inputs, 34-40 px tap targets, toast clamps) with every test still green, while a legitimate refactor of the blocks fails them and looks like loosening.
merged.recommendedFix: S1 contract: pair each pinned rule with an e2e computed-style or bounding-box check in ui-layout.spec or hud-layout.spec (at 390×844 touch, input font size ≥ 16 px and speed segments at least 34×40; at 360 px wide, at least 30; desktop warning titles clamp at 4 lines; short-landscape toast stack geometry). Mark the source-text tests as implementation pins in their headers and update a pin only together with its CSS while the paired e2e check stays green. Update design §20.3 to say fix-hud-toasts.test.ts:96 is superseded on phones by the nav.css rule plus its e2e geometry check. Leave ui-notify-news.test.ts's copy-sync check alone.

merged.title: S3-B's quiet hours and rate limits run on the device clock; without pinned time, notification tests will pass by day and fail at night
merged.summary: Quiet hours (22:00-08:00 on the device clock) and real-time rate limits will be unit-tested, but nothing requires injecting the clock or pinning the time zone. An unattended relaunch at night would send a time-of-day failure into repair, and a same-hour re-run fails the same way. The §12.7 forecast is deferred.
merged.recommendedFix: Add to the S3-B contract and NOTIFY acceptance: “Quiet-hour and rate-limit rules are pure functions of an injected now and the local minutes of the day; only the delivery adapter reads the clock. Unit tests cover 21:59, 22:00, 07:59, 08:00 and the midnight wrap without touching global time; integration code uses vi.setSystemTime; e2e uses Playwright's page.clock and a fixed timezoneId. Record the time zone in the evidence.” Add ‘no test outcome depends on the wall clock or the host time zone’ to the code-architecture role (protected; ADR).

merged.title: A whole-tank sale relocates the unlisted animals without a capacity limit and accepts high-risk mixes
merged.summary: findRelocation skips only incompatible tanks: stocking lowers a tank's score but never blocks it, high-risk mixes are allowed with a warning, and the combined load of several relocated animals is never re-checked (only a small per-animal penalty). It's a documented fallback for a sale the player started, and buyOffer also allows overstocking, so it matters mainly if S3 automation reuses it, where the master requires respecting tank capacity.
merged.recommendedFix: In S3, with S3-C's sell step: rank tanks with room first; check the cumulative load of every animal relocated in one sale (count load units, not animals); allow going over capacity only as a flagged last resort; automation paths must block outright. A hard block for player-started sales would make won auctions fail, so that part is the owner's call. Test: one nearly full tank and several unlisted animals end up spread out or flagged, never silently overstocked.

merged.title: Entering a show and withdrawing for a full refund still completes the ‘Enter a show’ quest ($60 and 4 reputation, once)
merged.summary: enterShow bumps show_entries; withdrawEntry refunds the fee in full and never decrements it; q_first_show is a relative counter quest. It isn't repeatable, so the exploit is a one-time $60 plus 4 reputation.
merged.recommendedFix: Backlog for S4 hardening: bump show_entries when entries close (at the deadline) for each entry still entered, or keep the bump and refuse a full refund once a quest has credited it; don't decrement a counter that only goes up. Test: enter then withdraw before the deadline leaves show_entries unchanged and the quest incomplete.

merged.title: Background LOD chunks lose events that happen inside a chunk: opening a far tank can rot a fresh meal, cool-water spawning cues vanish, and no test pins LOD equivalence
merged.summary: When a far tank (past the twelfth) becomes the focused one, its whole debt of 2-4 hours is stepped as one full-fidelity piece, and pieces are split around fresh food only for background LODs, so the meal rots before anyone eats (probe: mean hunger 70 → 79 instead of 55, ammonia 0.225 instead of 0.063 ppm); nearer tanks, with under an hour of debt, barely notice. The ‘first cool rains’ cue reads the temperature at the end of each piece, so a heater that recovers within a 1-4 hour chunk erases the drop: the cue fails for tanks past the twelfth and whenever the tick budget forces 1-hour chunks (it fires with half-hour smoothing). The step-size tests stop at 0.5 h and the LOD test checks only bookkeeping; no LOD tolerance is defined. No deaths or save damage, but S3 automation depends on step-size invariance.
merged.recommendedFix: Before S3 (LOD-fidelity question): 1) world.ts:128: also split pieces around fresh food at full LOD when the piece is longer than MAX_SUBSTEP_HOURS (normal full-LOD steps of 0.25 h are unaffected). 2) Record the lowest temperature seen within each piece (a transient field) and have the breeding cue use the lower of that and the end temperature; or cap background pieces at 0.5 h after a recent water change (the fresh-food pattern). 3) Add tests/sim/core-lod-equivalence.test.ts: the same tank at full fidelity in 0.025 h steps, reduced in 1 h chunks and summary in 4 h chunks over 96 h through real tank placement in advanceWorld, comparing hunger, health, ammonia, nitrate and survivors within tolerances recorded in OPERATIONS §11; plus a cool-cue test at every LOD and a focus-switch meal test. 4) Soften ARCHITECTURE.md:47 (M18). Seeded results may move: follow §11's protocol.

merged.title: mutateFast's working-copy contract is unenforced: store writes during a recipe are lost, nested calls drop work, and catch-up highlights leak the private working copy
merged.summary: publish() checks for an outside change to the store only when the recipe changed something; otherwise it records the other writer's state while the working copy still mirrors the old one, so the next mutateFast reverts it. A recipe's work is discarded if anything writes the store mid-recipe, and a nested mutateFast loses the outer work. simulateOffline's highlights are the working copy's own log objects, handed to useResume and a DOM event. No recipe does any of this today; 0.5 world-step hooks could.
merged.recommendedFix: Before S3's world-step hooks (or in S1): in publish(), check once, before sharing, whether the store changed during the recipe and drop the working copy on both paths; a module-level in-recipe flag makes a nested mutateFast throw; when the store changed during a recipe, report it (reportError or console.error) instead of dropping work silently; clone the highlights inside simulateOffline. Correct the header's ‘never lost’ claim and list the recipe constraints (sim code only, no store writes or nested calls, return plain values) in the fastMutate JSDoc and ARCHITECTURE.md. Add unit tests for the three cases.

merged.title: Accessibility gaps against design §18: unnamed dialogs, offer status hidden from screen readers, a welcome card without Esc, colour-only stability, mixed tab patterns, and high contrast that leaves panels translucent
merged.summary: The kit Modal is a dialog with no accessible name; offer cards' accessible name drops ‘Can't afford yet’, ‘Needs a … tank’, ‘Locked’ and ‘Leaving soon’; the welcome-back card has no Esc path; the kit Chip always sets aria-pressed, so one-shot dose chips read as unpressed toggles; stability shows a number with its verdict in colour only; kit Tabs and Segmented lack arrow keys while the panels' Seg has them. High contrast (‘Solid panels and brighter text’) overrides only HUD glass and text tokens, so panels keep 0.035-alpha cards, 0.1-alpha borders and blur, and the spec gives the new tab bar literal colours. All of this predates the harness.
merged.recommendedFix: Add ACC requirements (M07) and fix in S1 and S2 per §18: Modal names itself through useId and a Panel titleId for aria-labelledby; fold blocking status into the offer card's name or aria-describedby (or drop the button role in S2's card redesign); add the welcome card to GameHUD's Escape chain, without forcing focus; Chip emits aria-pressed only when selected is defined; stability shows a word using the 60/30 thresholds; kit Tabs gets arrow keys and roving tabindex, and Segmented matches. High contrast: a new CSS file overriding, under the high-contrast attribute, the panel card, card-hover, card-line (about the strength of the general line token) and sheet background (the strong glass token), the panel switcher, and the sheet's backdrop blur; nav.css uses the glass and line tokens, with an erratum replacing the §5.2 literal. A static test checks every colour-valued panel token has a high-contrast value. The target level is the owner's question.

merged.title: Errors swallowed inside mutate recipes commit half-applied actions, against the code's own rule
merged.summary: act.ts and actions.ts say errors must escape the recipe so Immer discards the draft, yet TutorialCoach, the photo story and actions.ts's tutorial step catch errors inside the recipe, and PlacementGhost catches around buyTank, whose spend runs before createTank, so a throw would commit the money with no tank. edit() has no catch, so a throw inside Listings' 15-second hold interval would surface as an uncaught error every 15 seconds. Nothing throws on these paths today.
merged.recommendedFix: In S1, which touches these files anyway: wrap the mutate call, not the mutator (e.g. run the tutorial skip mutate inside safe()); run actions.ts's tutorial advance in a second mutate after the main action commits, with its own try around that mutate; drop the inner safe() in story.ts and guard PhotoMode's mutate; move PlacementGhost's try/catch outside mutate (or route it through act()); give edit() a logging catch and guard the Listings interval call. Unit test per wrapper: a mutator that changes the draft and then throws leaves the game state unchanged.

merged.title: Far-tank AI cost grows with tanks × animals, steps every far tank on the same frame, and keeps stepping tanks that are hidden
merged.summary: Far tanks step on a time accumulator with no frame-budget check and identical starting values, so they all step on the same frame (about 1.8 ms every third frame on big_facility: 15 tanks, 337 animals); every store version bump makes each TankAI scan all creatures and clutches (about 0.64 ms); tanks hidden in tank view keep stepping. Small on desktop and unmeasured on phones; S3's scale increases both.
merged.recommendedFix: Backlog with an S3 performance scenario (facility-size question): give each tank's accumulator a stable phase offset derived from its id; make the far branch respect the AI frame budget; throttle, rather than freeze, hidden tanks; build one creatures-and-clutches-by-tank index per store version shared by all TankAIs. The AI is presentation only, so sim determinism is unaffected.

merged.title: The portrait cache is never evicted and its blob URLs are never revoked
merged.summary: Every rendered portrait (species, appearance, life stage, sex and size) stays in a module-level Map as a blob URL, and clearPortraitCache has no caller. They're small WebP thumbnails, so a long session reaches tens of MB at worst; S2 and S3 add portrait-heavy lists.
merged.recommendedFix: Backlog for S2 (fishart lane): an LRU cap of about 300-500 that evicts only keys with no live subscriber and revokes their blob URLs; refresh recency on cache hits; make clearPortraitCache skip subscribed keys (or re-request and notify them). Unit test: the cache stays at or under the cap after N distinct requests, and a subscribed key survives. Don't clear on a new save or on pagehide.

merged.title: Per-frame code still allocates, DecorItem scans every tank per anemone, and nothing guards against new per-frame allocations
merged.summary: A scan of all 51 per-frame callbacks found objects, template strings, filtered arrays, Sets and spreads created every frame, plus a scan of every tank's creatures for each anemone or host coral every frame. It's minor garbage-collection pressure today, and no lint or probe catches new cases.
merged.recommendedFix: Backlog for S1's render pass: add a non-allocating hasRecentEvent(tankId, since, kinds); a per-tank creature index for DecorItem; scratch objects instead of key strings in CameraRig; in-place compaction instead of filter reassignments; reused scratch Sets and arrays in staffRuntime; a boolean ref in SceneRoot. Promote the frame scan to an advisory `npm run qa:frame-alloc` (TypeScript compiler API only) and list it in the performance role.

merged.title: Facility InstancedMeshes are never disposed, so their instance buffers are orphaned on every layout rebuild
merged.summary: LightPools, Products, Books and ColumnWashes rebuild InstancedMeshes in useMemo and render them as primitives; their cleanups dispose only the geometry, and React Three Fiber never disposes primitives, so instance matrix and colour buffers wait for garbage collection after each place, move, sale or re-tier.
merged.recommendedFix: In the next render-touching slice: dispose the instanced meshes alongside the geometry in each cleanup effect (LightPools: pools and washes; Products, Books and ColumnWashes: the mesh), with the meshes in the effect dependencies. Safe under StrictMode. A GPU-memory metric (M37) would catch regressions.

merged.title: TankAI creates its world and food registry during render but its cleanup deletes them, so a re-run effect (StrictMode or <Activity>) leaves the tank empty
merged.summary: Latent: StrictMode is off and <Activity> isn't used, but hiding far tanks with <Activity> is a natural fix for M80. A re-run effect would drop the tank's food registry and leave its animals missing until the next store version bump, which never comes while the game is paused.
merged.recommendedFix: When TankAI is next touched: in the effect body, register the tank's food array again and reset the mirrored version (e.g. to −1) so the next frame re-mirrors, and drop the render-phase registration. Unit test: run the cleanup, re-run the effect, and assert the food registry has the tank and the animals return without a version bump.

merged.title: The approved 0.5 visual reference (45 static screens) lives only in a private canvas, so QA can't check ‘screenshot fidelity’ from the repo
merged.summary: DESIGN_INTAKE requires every new design to be captured in the repo with exported screens and a source note, but DESIGN-0.5 was registered as approved without them, and the browser-qa role still asks for screenshot fidelity. The written spec wins on conflict (§3.9).
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides (question). If yes: export to docs/agent/design/DESIGN-0.5/ (screens named <screen>-<state>-<viewport>.png; a SOURCE.md with the export date and SHA-256 of each file; a manifest mapping each screen to its Appendix A row, route and test ids), and add the screens path to the registry entry (ADR and reviewer). Until then, add to the browser-qa role (owner-approved prompt change): “Judge fidelity against the written spec and Appendix A; where no repo screen exists, record ‘visual reference unavailable’ as a limitation, never as a pass or a guess.”

merged.title: The master puts production and the undesigned S3-D before Social and whole-stack hardening, which the design had last and allowed to slip
merged.summary: This is the owner's deliberate order (master §9, recorded in the registry and ADR-0003), and a stalled S3 stops at an owner gate rather than looping. But ADR-0002's ‘S3 cannot be accepted without S3-D (master §45)’ attributes to §45 a coupling it doesn't state, and a late S3-D design or a blocked S3 would hold back the Social stub and the whole-stack hardening.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides (question). If S4 may go ahead while S3-D waits: one ADR adds the transition (or a separate S5 for S3-D plus a re-hardening pass before the Multiplayer Readiness Gate) and changes master §9 (‘five mega-slices’), §10, OPERATIONS §4 (the S4-only route to the readiness gate), lib.mjs SLICES and the harness tests together. Either way, the next ADR rewords ADR-0002's sentence to “S3 cannot be accepted without S3-D under the current slice boundaries (master §9)”.

merged.title: Rarity-tier inflation (466 of 540 betta morphs Legendary) is an open owner decision the master turned into reviewer judgement
merged.summary: The design says ‘Decide before Phase 2 ships’; master §42 only has S2 reproduce the numbers and a reviewer inspect them, with ‘an ADR and owner-visible explanation’ for a change, so S2 could advance with the question unanswered. ADR-0003 lists it as an open owner question. v0.4.0 already shows 170 of 240 betta entries as Legendary; tiers are computed at run time, not saved.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides before S2 (question) and the answer is recorded verbatim in an ADR naming which design-pinned numbers change. Add a GEN requirement for the chosen model and the distribution report the S2 reviewer must attach. Owner-approved master §42 edit: ‘owner-visible explanation’ → ‘owner approval at OWNER_GATE’; a reviewer who finds the hierarchy uninformative returns YELLOW, not GREEN.

merged.title: The approved ‘notifications unsupported’ copy tells iPhone players to add the game to their Home Screen, which the design's own risk list says won't work in this build
merged.summary: There's no web-app manifest or Apple web-app meta tag, so the design's own risk list says iOS web notifications won't work. A Home Screen web app also gets storage separate from Safari's, so a player following the advice would open a game without their save. ADR-0003 lists this as an open owner question; NOTIFY-001 is in S3.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides before S3-B (question). Recommended: replace the copy with “This browser can't show notifications” / “Alerts still appear in the game.”, record the decision verbatim in an ADR, apply it as a §12.3 erratum, and add a NOTIFY-001 acceptance line for the unsupported-state copy. A Home Screen hint would need a manifest, icons, a test on a current iPhone and a separate-save warning (which needs save export and import).

merged.title: Design §12.2's event sources are partly wrong: the new-species stocking event isn't a ‘rare strain’ event, and there's no ‘auction ending soon’ event although the Settings copy promises one
merged.summary: stockNewUnlocks announces up to three new-species offers in one event, so a single offer id is ill-defined; listings only emit events after an auction ends (‘ended without a sale’, ‘Bidding closed on …’). The approved subtitle ‘New bids, sales and auctions ending’ names an event nothing produces.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides on ‘auction ending soon’ (question). Erratum either way: “stockNewUnlocks sets an offer id only when it stocks exactly one offer (or the Prismatic one); otherwise the event opens #/shop, and it is categorised as ‘new species’, not rare stock. maybeSpecial maps with its offer id.” Without the new event: subtitle → “New bids, sales and closed auctions”, mapping ‘Bidding closed on {title}’ (which carries the listing id). With it: one deterministic event per listing a few game hours before the end, only when there are open bids, routed to the listing, with a test.

merged.title: Production builds ship full state-editing developer tools (window.__AQ, a permanent ?dev=1, fixture autosave, sandboxes), and the Multiplayer gate has no trust-boundary criteria
merged.summary: debugHooks is imported unconditionally, so the production bundle carries mutate, setGame, act, add money, unlock all, make Prismatic, import text and delete save on window.__AQ; ?dev=1 turns dev mode on permanently; Settings offers ‘Developer tools’ to every player; ?fixture=…&autosave=1 writes a fixture into the player's autosave; ?sandbox= and debug globals ship. In a local single-player game this is a documented feature rather than a hole, and the writes go through the store boundary, but any value a future leaderboard ranks can be set from the console, and the master's ‘clean trust boundary for future server authority’ has no criteria.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides what developer tooling ships (question). Agent-doable now: add criteria to the Multiplayer Readiness Gate in master §10 (owner ADR): “No client-computed value is trusted for leaderboards, trades or the economy; uploaded snapshots are parsed by a hardened parser and recomputed or validated on a server; developer write surfaces are absent from the production bundle; the security-data reviewer signs off.” Cheap and behaviour-preserving: make ?dev=1 last only for the session (don't persist it from the URL), ignore &autosave=1 outside dev and QA builds, and note ‘developer tools ship in production’ in KNOWN_LIMITATIONS. If __AQ's writes are gated, check the DEV flag or a ?dev URL parameter at import time (keeping read-only diagnostics), and pass ?dev=1 in qa-shots and any preview-based e2e run.

merged.title: Saves, settings, notification permission and the planned service worker sit on the shared graygrayson1.github.io origin
merged.summary: All GitHub Pages project sites of the account share one origin and idb-keyval's default database. Today the only co-tenants are the owner's own two static sites (no IndexedDB or service worker, no user site), so the risk is latent; it grows when S3-B adds a service worker and notification permission and when S4 or later stores an email or token. Render is a separate origin with separate saves.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides the main origin before any real account or token (question). S3-B acceptance (agent-doable): the service worker registers at the base URL with that scope, and its notification click handler filters matched windows to URLs under its own scope before focusing one or posting a route. Backlog: a namespaced IndexedDB store with a read-old/write-new migration (core sign-off), noting it isn't a security boundary. Moving origins needs save export and import, or a one-time migration, first.

merged.title: The Social stub's sign-in form invites real passwords that browsers may save for a shared origin, and it stores the email
merged.summary: The designed form uses a password field marked current-password, accepts any address-shaped email with 8 or more characters and says ‘Signed in’; the ‘prototype’ hint shows only in dev mode; localStorage keeps the email, display name and joined clubs. SOC-002 only forbids storing the password. Nothing is built yet (S4).
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides how Social appears in a release (question). Recommended, keeping the spec's test ids and the signIn(email, password) interface: a visible “Preview: no real account. Don't use a real password.” label in all builds; autocomplete off on the stub's password field; store only the display name and joined clubs (or a masked email); extend SOC-002 so that after sign-in no stored value contains the typed password or the full email. Record the decision in an S4 design ADR.

merged.title: The GitHub deploy workflow and Render build run no tests before publishing
merged.summary: After an approved push nothing remote re-runs the unit suite; typecheck runs only through the build's tsc step. The local gates are the release gate, so this is defence in depth. .github and render.yaml are deploy and gate-defining files.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides (question). If yes: a local commit adding an `npm test` step after `npm ci` in deploy.yml and `npm ci && npm test && npm run build` as render.yaml's build command, under an ADR with independent review and listed in the owner package; relaunch.mjs will flag the deploy-config change, as expected. Keep e2e local (the Playwright config uses macOS Metal flags).

merged.title: Morph names and catalog odds disagree with what the game produces: a bristlenose name collision, rare morphs stocked more often than ‘1 in n’, and encyclopedia names the genetics never make
merged.summary: composeMorphName drops repeated words, so ‘Super Red’ with ‘Super Long-fin’ gets the same name as ‘Super Red’ with ‘Long-fin’: one name, one discovery and one tier for two looks. Catalog tiers are Hardy–Weinberg shares, but rare and special single offers pick the most striking of six rolls, so some rare morphs are stocked up to about 2.4× more often than the ‘about 1 in n’ the 0.5 design will print (5 of 62 rare betta rows would change tier). Some encyclopedia visualMorphs names (e.g. ‘Red Cap Oranda’) may be real-world reference names rather than in-game ones.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides before S2 (question). Recommended: rename the bristlenose overlay in data (e.g. ‘Long-fin’ and ‘Double Long-fin’) with a renamedMorphs migration for existing saves; add a data test that no catalog entry merges two different phenotypes (and rule on the cherry shrimp merges it finds); label catalog odds ‘of ordinary market stock’ or compute the share including the seller's pick; decide whether visualMorphs are reference names.

merged.title: Animals in the holding container are frozen in time, though the game tells the player to ‘give them a tank soon’
merged.summary: The tank-sale fallback and save repair move animals into holding (no tank); the world step only steps tanks, so holding animals don't eat, age or die (probe: ten game days with stats unchanged), and the warning's urgency is untrue.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides (question). Recommended default: honest stasis. Reword the listings.ts message to “… is resting in a holding container (they don't eat or age there). Move them to a tank when you can.”, match the Livestock row label, add a KNOWN_LIMITATIONS line, and prefer relocating at sale time where possible.

merged.title: Moving a placed tank is unreachable: the room view reads a ‘move:<id>’ panel target that nothing writes
merged.summary: The placement ghost and tool rail read panelTarget ‘move:<tankId>’, but no code has ever written it; the sim's placeTank is tested and exposed through __AQ. S1's router will treat panelTarget as a one-shot panel command.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides (question). To keep it: add a ‘Move tank’ action (tank card or Tanks panel) backed by its own UI field, with an e2e test. To drop it: delete only the UI move branches (PlacementGhost's move paths, the ToolRail text and the header comment), keep the sim's placeTank and its tests, and log the feature in BACKLOG. Either way the S1 contract says panelTarget carries panel commands only.

merged.title: 46 react-hooks/exhaustive-deps suppressions exist with no linter installed, and one FoodPicker memo is stale
merged.summary: The suppression comments imply a check that doesn't exist. ToolRail's foodOptions memo omits creatures and clutches, so an open food picker's ‘who eats this’ lags arrivals and life-stage changes. S1's router adds many effects and subscriptions.
merged.recommendedFix: Owner decides on a dev-only ESLint with the React hooks plugin (new devDependencies need an ADR and approval; question). Meanwhile, in S1, fix the memo: drop it (foodOptions is cheap) or key it on a derived signature (resident ids and species plus clutch ids and stages through a shallow selector), and check the sibling alert memo. Note in the S1 contract that hook dependencies are reviewed by hand.

merged.title: Sanitising turns a non-finite health into 0, so a future NaN bug would kill animals silently
merged.summary: The clamp helper maps NaN to its lower bound, and at step.ts:976 that happens just before the death check, so a NaN health would show up as a death from ‘declining health’. No NaN source exists today (a fuzz run was clean); save repair uses neutral defaults instead.
merged.recommendedFix: S4 hardening backlog: give health its own guard at step.ts:976 and in sanitize: a non-finite value becomes the last finite health when there is one, otherwise a neutral default (90, as in migrations), never 0, with a dev-only console warning; turn the NaN fuzz probe into a tests/sim case asserting no death from injected NaN.

merged.title: Verified clean: entropy stays out of the sim, saves round-trip losslessly, repairState is idempotent, and nothing in public/ conflicts with a service worker
merged.summary: Math.random and Date.now appear only in new-game seeding, persistence timestamps and slot ids, and the loop and autosave timers; wall-clock fields are excluded from the state hash; encode/decode is hash-identical across 11 fixtures over 240 game hours; repairState is idempotent (a second pass finds nothing) for a fresh game, a legacy v0 save and big_facility; non-finite numbers become 0 at save; public/ holds only favicon.svg and version.json is generated at build time.
merged.recommendedFix: No action. Lock these in as PERSIST-002 regression tests (repairState twice gives an equal state hash; two round trips keep the hash for a fresh game, legacy v0 and big_facility; extend to an S3 production fixture). In S3-B the service worker must never cache version.json.

merged.title: Verified compliant: AI never writes eating outcomes back, render subscriptions are narrow, AI loops are capped and audio cleans up
merged.summary: Apart from TankAI's tutorial observed:* write (M13), AI code calls no mutate and only reads food from the sim; at most two AI steps run per frame and step size is clamped; no render selector subscribes to the whole game; one AudioContext, gesture listeners removed, microphone tracks stopped, voices capped.
merged.recommendedFix: No action. Add one line to ARCHITECTURE.md: “AI results such as eating are never written back to the sim; the sim shares food out, and the AI only animates it.”

merged.title: Verified: listing anti-duplication protections hold; S3 auto-listing must go through createListing and quickSell only
merged.summary: Listed, sold or dead animals and animals in a whole-tank listing are refused; completeSale re-validates before paying; acceptBid re-checks integrity and the amount; frags are de-duplicated; quickSellQuote refuses listed animals; carried broods leave with a sold carrier. No double-sell or double-list path was found.
merged.recommendedFix: No code action. Add to the S3-C and S3-D contracts: “Automation creates listings only through createListing and sells only through quickSell or completeSale; it never writes listings or statuses directly, and it respects the 24-listing cap by pausing with a notice.”

questions.question: Do you ratify ADR-0003, the harness revision this review produced?
questions.why: Your revised harness says only you change the master, OPERATIONS.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README_FIRST.md and the prompts, with your words recorded verbatim (master §54, OPERATIONS §10). ADR-0003 changed all of them on the strength of your general request to improve things, and it is marked Accepted. It adds seven rules: a cap of 5 attempts per defect with a reviewer judging whether strategies differ; YELLOW never advances on its own; protected files change only by ADR; gate and deploy files need an ADR and a reviewer; no commits on main and local main stays equal to origin/main; at an owner gate, park the item, keep working on the rest, then stop; no schema bump until you decide. It also defines what counts as your approval, sets requirement decomposition at design-subsection level, and ends S0 with your review (S0-T12). Until you ratify it, a fresh agent can't tell whether these rules carry your authority.
options: Ratify ADR-0003 as written, rules 1-7 included
Ratify with exceptions you name (for example the YELLOW rule or the 5-attempt cap)
Hold it and decide at S0-T12 from a one-page summary
questions.recommendation: Ratify at S0-T12 from a one-page summary, and decide the YELLOW rule explicitly (separate question). Your answer goes verbatim into ADR-0004, which also replaces ADR-0002's line saying a STATE.json flag can count as your decision.

questions.question: May we put technical guards on pushes and deploys, which you install and lift yourself?
questions.why: In attended sessions (your default) only written rules stop a push. gh is on the agent's PATH and the repo's credential helper uses it, so git push would authenticate; main has no branch protection and the github-pages environment has no reviewer; the Render and Vercel CLIs are logged in and the Vercel plugin is on. A push to main deploys GitHub Pages, and because render.yaml says autoDeploy: true it may deploy Render too. The unattended launcher already denies these commands, but agents may not change their own permissions.
options: A: Disable origin's push URL (git config remote.origin.pushurl no-push://owner-approval-required); add per-machine ask rules in .claude/settings.local.json for git push, gh write commands, render, vercel and npm publish (they prompt you, and unattended runs treat them as deny); turn the Vercel plugin off for this project; protect main on GitHub or add a required reviewer to the github-pages environment
B: Local guards only (push URL plus ask rules), no GitHub change
C: Hard deny rules (these also block pushes you approve from Claude; you'd push from a terminal)
D: Keep written rules only
questions.recommendation: A. Everything is reversible: git config --unset remote.origin.pushurl when you approve a push.

questions.question: How should e2e tests and browser QA run, given headless Chromium can't start inside Claude Code's sandboxed shell?
questions.why: On 2026-10-05 npm run e2e hung at browser launch in the sandbox (baseline failure BF-001), so the baseline e2e status is unknown. S0 can't meet its e2e acceptance criterion, and every user-visible slice needs a browser-QA review that would have to report RED. Agents can't grant themselves a sandbox exception.
options: A: Allow a narrow sandbox exception for the test commands only (npm run e2e, npx playwright test, npm run qa:shots) in your Claude Code settings
B: You run e2e and browser QA yourself at each slice boundary, and agents record your output as evidence
C: Browser gates run only in sessions you start without the sandbox (for example the relaunch launcher, configured by you)
D: Accept e2e as not run for now (S0 and UI slices then can't be accepted under the current rules)
questions.recommendation: A, with B as the fallback. Then record a real baseline e2e run at 0d9fc5a.

questions.question: When a test was already failing or flaky before any work, what may its gate count as once you acknowledge it?
questions.why: Acceptance needs every gate GREEN, meaning exit 0 on the checkpoint code, so an acknowledged pre-existing failure still blocks forever. The only way out today is marking the gate NOT_APPLICABLE, which needs no justification. Skipping, loosening or retrying tests to get green is forbidden.
options: A: Strict: every gate must pass; acknowledged failures block until fixed

B: Per-test acknowledgement: the failing test ids are listed with your ADR; no new failures, no new skips and no drop in test counts; the gate gets a distinct value (KNOWN_BASELINE) shown in every acceptance report; the list may only shrink; a functional (non-timing) failure still stops for you before S1
C: Treat acknowledged failures as GREEN
questions.recommendation: B. Also require a cited ADR before typecheck, unit, build, e2e or a harness gate can be marked NOT_APPLICABLE, and keep the rule of one recorded re-run for flakes (OPERATIONS §6).

questions.question: What must the save format guarantee for players' existing v0.4.0 saves, and may the build ever bump SCHEMA_VERSION?
questions.why: ADR-0001 says old-save compatibility is best-effort; the design says no bump and requires a v0.4.0 save to load with no repairs after every phase. The live v0.4.0 code treats a newer-schema save as damaged, restores an older backup and then overwrites the newer save, and deployed code can't be patched. The S0 revision made a bump an owner gate and added requirements PERSIST-001 and PERSIST-003, which go further than ADR-0001 without your approval.
options: A: Strict for 0.5: SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1, only optional additive fields, and a committed v0.4.0 save loads with no repairs at every slice

B: v0.4.0 saves must keep loading; a bump is allowed only with your approval at an owner gate, under a new storage key prefix, after a build that never falls back past a too-new save has shipped, with migration tests
C: Best-effort as ADR-0001 says: agents may bump and drop old saves if needed
questions.recommendation: A for 0.5, with B's conditions written down for any later bump. Either way, the 0.5 code should stop falling back past a too-new save (PERSIST-003).

questions.question: Where should the local work be backed up after each accepted checkpoint?
questions.why: The repo lives in a removable disk image on the external drive, Time Machine has no destination, and pushing is forbidden, so every S0-S4 commit, piece of evidence and decision would exist in one place. A bundle of the repo is about 14 MB.
options: A: git bundle --all to a folder on the internal disk after each checkpoint (stays on this Mac)
B: The same bundle to another drive or a cloud-synced folder you name
C: Push the integration branch to a new private GitHub repo with no workflows after each checkpoint (a standing approval for that repo only)
D: No backup
questions.recommendation: A or B in a folder you choose, added to the checkpoint procedure with the bundle's hash recorded as evidence. Also consider giving Time Machine a destination for the Dev image.

questions.question: Can a mega-slice with a YELLOW verdict (an accepted limitation with no contract violation) advance without you?
questions.why: ADR-0003 rule 2 says an unrepaired YELLOW always needs your approval in an ADR, while the master still says your approval is needed only if the limitation changes owner-visible behaviour. Strict rules stop the build more often; loose ones let the orchestrator accept its own limitations.
options: A: Never: every unrepaired YELLOW stops at an owner gate (ADR-0003 rule 2)

B: A limitation you wouldn't notice may advance with an independent reviewer's written agreement and an ADR listing it; anything you'd notice (copy, screens, mechanics, economy numbers, scope) stops for you
C: Treat YELLOW like GREEN with notes
questions.recommendation: B, with that definition of 'would notice' written into OPERATIONS §2.

questions.question: When a simulation step keeps failing with an error, what should the player see?
questions.why: Ticks are now all-or-nothing in the working tree, so a persistent error no longer corrupts the save, but the world silently freezes: the clock stops, a message appears only in the console, and the player isn't told.
options: A: After 3 consecutive failed ticks, pause and show a persistent banner ('The simulation hit an error and is paused. Your last save is intact.') with Export a copy and Reload
B: Keep retrying silently
C: Skip only the failing subsystem for that tick and carry on, with a notice
questions.recommendation: A now; consider C later for non-critical subsystems such as shows and visitors.

questions.question: When the player leaves a game (loads another save, returns to the title, presses Reload on the update prompt, or uses the crash screen's Save & reload) with Autosave off, or the save fails, what should happen?
questions.why: These paths can drop unsaved play silently today. With Autosave off nothing is saved, although the Load confirmation says it is, and failed saves are ignored on Return to title and on the crash screen.
options: A: Always save on these exits, whatever the Autosave setting; if the save fails, stay in the game and offer Retry, Export a copy and 'Leave without saving'
B: Respect Autosave off, but ask 'Leave without saving? Last save: <time>' and make the copy true
C: Respect it silently and only fix the copy
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: How should factual errors in the approved design spec and the master be corrected?
questions.why: This review found about 15 places where the approved design describes today's code wrongly (router targets, toast placement, genetics visibility, notification events, verdict labels). The master's Design Change Gate is heavyweight, and only you approve designs.
options: A: A full Design Change Gate for every correction

B: Lightweight errata: each records the old text, the new text and the code evidence in BACKLOG.md, an independent reviewer confirms it, and it is applied through the slice contract; any erratum that changes copy, screens or mechanics a player would notice comes to you at slice planning
C: Leave the spec untouched and let slice contracts override it silently
questions.recommendation: B.

questions.question: When should existing architecture debt be paid down?
questions.why: The review found research gates enforced only in the UI, game-rule code living in src/ui, UI copies of simulation formulas that have drifted, species and food rules hard-coded outside the data files, and 10 exceptions to the import rules. ADR-0001 allows refactors only when a requirement drives them and they are tested and recorded, and S0 is named 'Architecture Lock'.
options: A: Fix all of it in S0

B: In S0, add only the guards (a traced architecture requirement, boundary tests with frozen allowlists, checks on where state is written) and the clear bug fixes (water-class gates enforced in the simulation, the drifted UI numbers); each refactor lands with an ADR in the slice that first touches its area
C: Put everything in the backlog and fix only what blocks a slice
questions.recommendation: B.

questions.question: Do the old lane boundaries still limit which non-core files a builder may edit?
questions.why: The approved design says 'Edit only the files your lane owns', but the harness uses a single builder, and ownership now exists only as OWNER: headers in 464 of 562 source files. Master §3.8 covers only core-owned files.
options: A: Informational only: a builder may edit any file its approved slice contract lists, and core and gate-defining files keep §3.8's conditions
B: Each task names the lanes it touches and stays inside them
C: Retire lanes and remove the headers over time
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: How should screenshots be handled, both as evidence and for S1's 'baseline visual snapshots'?
questions.why: The master asks S1 for baseline visual snapshots without defining them, forbids regenerating snapshots blindly, and keeps binary evidence out of Git until you decide. qa:shots overwrites the 14 tracked PNGs by default, and pixel comparisons of an animated WebGL scene would be flaky.
options: A: Evidence only: screenshots go to .agent-runs with their hashes in the manifest; screenshots/ is refreshed only at release; S1's baselines are hashed qa:shots sets reviewed by Browser QA, not a pixel gate
B: Commit screenshots and traces as evidence
C: A, plus gating pixel checks on a few stable DOM-only screens (title, settings, shop list) with the 3D canvas masked; their baselines change only by ADR
questions.recommendation: C.

questions.question: May agents export the private design canvas's 45 static screens, and later the S3-D designs, into the repo?
questions.why: QA is asked to check screenshot fidelity, but the only copy of the approved screens is a private claude.ai canvas that other or headless agents can't open, and the repository is meant to be the project's memory.
options: A: Yes: export them as PNGs to docs/agent/design/DESIGN-0.5/screens with a source note and hashes; the written spec still wins on any conflict
B: No: QA judges fidelity against the written spec only
C: Export them but keep them out of Git on this machine
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: Design §6.4 (S1): which links skip the title screen, what does reload (F5) do, and what does the loading card show?
questions.why: After S1 almost every URL carries a hash ('#/' after closing a panel), so 'opened from a link' would skip the title for bookmarks and address-bar visits. The spec's reason for returning to the title on reload (protecting tests) is wrong, so this is purely a player-experience choice. A real progress bar would need a change to the core catch-up code.
options: A: A deep link is a hash that names a real screen; empty, '#/' and unknown hashes show the title; F5 returns to the title; the loading card shows an indeterminate bar with the time away read from the save
B: Reload keeps your place: load the latest save and reopen the screen
C: Never auto-load; show the title with 'Continue to {destination}'
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: What should the e2e gate run against: the dev server, a production build, or both?
questions.why: The gates test only the dev server at '/'. GitHub Pages serves a minified build under /aquarium-go/, and S3-B's service worker and S1's Copy link depend on that path.
options: A: The dev server only (today)
B: The full suite on the dev server, plus a production-preview smoke test under /aquarium-go/, required from S1
C: A production preview only
questions.recommendation: B.

questions.question: Should automated gates cover phones held sideways, and WebKit (the iOS Safari engine)?
questions.why: All 47 e2e tests run in Chromium. Only 4 cover phone portrait and 2 cover landscape (toasts only). The design puts the new tab bar on sideways phones, but the planned specs test portrait only.
options: A: Add 844×390 cases to the S1 phone specs, Chromium only
B: A, plus a small WebKit phone smoke project (a Playwright browser download, not an npm dependency)
C: Leave landscape and Safari to the manual browser-QA review
questions.recommendation: A now; B once the S1 navigation lands.

questions.question: How should timing-sensitive tests count toward slice acceptance?
questions.why: perf.spec, whose frame-rate and loop-time floors were calibrated on this Mac while idle, runs inside the functional e2e gate; two unit tests retry silently; and the machine is often busy with agents. No performance baseline exists yet, and the browser can't run in the sandbox.
options: A: A separate perf gate: perf.spec and the wall-clock budgets run alone on a quiet machine with the load recorded and are compared with a recorded baseline; the retries are removed; headless Node probes of AI and simulation cost count as per-slice evidence, and browser perf runs at slice boundaries
B: Keep them as hard Level 3 gates with a quiet-machine precondition
C: Keep them as they are, but allow one recorded re-run of a timing failure
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: What performance targets must hold: which device class, and how large a facility after S3?
questions.why: The only floors are 30/30/24 fps in headless Chromium on this Mac. The 0.5 design is phone-first, there is no phone or memory budget, and nothing says how many tanks and animals S3's automation must handle (far-tank AI cost grows with tanks × animals).
options: A: Today's Mac floors only; big_facility (15 tanks, about 340 animals) is the ceiling
B: Add a phone-like scenario (CPU throttling ×4 at 390×844) with its own floor and a no-growth budget for GPU resources; S3 must handle about twice big_facility (a new huge_facility fixture)
C: No fixed targets; the performance reviewer decides per slice
questions.recommendation: B, plus your own check on a real phone at S1 and S3 acceptance. Agents won't invent numeric budgets without your answer.

questions.question: What accessibility standard should the build meet, and should high contrast make the panels solid?
questions.why: Design §18 lists rules but sets no conformance target, and the requirements registry has no accessibility entries. Existing gaps include unnamed dialogs, offer status hidden from screen readers and inconsistent tab patterns. The High contrast setting promises 'Solid panels' but leaves the management panels translucent.
options: A: WCAG 2.2 AA for every new 0.5 surface, with known gaps fixed in S4 and tracked as requirements; high contrast makes panels, cards, the tab bar and the More sheet solid in S1
B: Only design §18's specific rules
C: A full AA audit of the whole app now
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: Are the design's 'optional' items required in this build?
questions.why: The design marks the share sheet, temperament meters in the breeding forecast and a Finances 'Automation gear' row as optional. The master's slice lists name nearby items ('share seam', 'breeding forecast integration', 'finances/upkeep') that turn out to be the mandatory parts. Without a ruling, the extras get built without a spec or flagged as dropped scope.
options: A: All optional items go to the backlog unless you name them
B: Build them all
C: Build the mandatory parts the master points to (copy link, the forecast with the new genes, upkeep) and record the three optional extras as deferred
questions.recommendation: C.

questions.question: How should betta rarity tiers work now that the expansion makes 466 of 540 morphs Legendary?
questions.why: The design says to decide before Phase 2 ships; the master only has a reviewer inspect it. Tiers feed the Rare genes filter, the card chips and leaderboards, and a later change ripples through tests pinned to exact numbers.
options: A: Keep the absolute thresholds (no engine change; the design's numbers stay valid)
B: Tier by share within each colour group (changes morphCatalog.ts and the pinned numbers)
C: Count only the names the market actually stocks
D: Retune the thresholds
questions.recommendation: Decide before S2. A, unless 'Legendary everywhere' bothers you; S2's reviewer attaches the distribution report either way.

questions.question: Should a betta that shows one trait but carries rare Opaque White or Double Tail at the same dominance count as a hidden carrier?
questions.why: Today a Yellow Crowntail carrying white and double reports nothing hidden, and its card says '(both expressed)' for traits that don't show, so the Rare genes filter would miss about 1-2% of market bettas.
options: A: Yes, by a data-only fix: put white and double below yellow and crown, so such fish 'carry' them and cards stop saying 'both expressed'
B: Yes, by changing the visibility rule (the filter helper and card wording) with no data change
C: No: keep the engine's current meaning
D: Remove the rare flag from white and double
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: S2's two new betta genes shift the random sequence for every seeded game. How should that be handled?
questions.why: The shift re-rolls the starter behind a seed-fragile show-balance test that fails for 7 of 20 other seeds, and the design wrongly says only one test depends on the seeded stream. Re-seeding or loosening tests looks like weakening them.
options: A: Accept the shift and re-baseline the seeded tests under the recorded before-and-after protocol (OPERATIONS §11)
B: Draw the new genes from a separate per-creature stream so existing seeded games and starters stay identical (a small genetics.ts change)
C: First harden the fragile tests (fixed starter potentials, clean water), then accept the shift
questions.recommendation: C, plus B only if the genetics reviewer agrees it isn't a restructure of the genetics engine.

questions.question: What should 'about 1 in n market {species}' mean for morphs, and may an existing morph name be renamed to fix a collision?
questions.why: Rare and special single offers pick the most striking of six rolls, so some rare morphs are stocked up to about 2.4× more often than the catalog says. A bristlenose naming rule gives two different looks the same name, and fixing it renames a morph in existing saves.
options: A: Compute the true stocking share, including the seller's pick
B: Keep the catalog odds and label them 'of ordinary market stock'
C: Remove the best-of-six pick so stock matches the catalog
Plus, separately: rename the colliding morph with a save migration, or leave it
questions.recommendation: B (or A if it's cheap), and rename with a save migration.

questions.question: Do quick sales to the local store count as 'sales', and does 'sales' count transactions or animals?
questions.why: Quick-selling 25 young shrimp for $27 now unlocks whole-tank auctions ('Make three sales'), earns 'Trusted Trader — Complete 25 sales' and about 40 reputation, and counts toward the 'Happy customer' quest (a buyer who will care for the animal). Frag store sales are deliberately excluded.
options: A: Count transactions only; store quick sales don't count toward sales reputation, quests or unlocks (like frag sales)
B: Count animals, but only for marketplace listings
C: Keep it as it is
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: Should a buyer ever pay more than their private ceiling or budget after counter-offers?
questions.why: Repeated small counters double a patient buyer's price (2.0× in about 90 rounds) with no risk of them walking away, and keep the listing open days after it ended, against the code's own rule that bids never ratchet upward.
options: A: Hard cap: never above the original ceiling × 1.03 or the buyer's budget; at most 3 counter rounds; no counters after the closing grace period
B: Allow a bounded premium (for example one round up to +10%)
C: Keep it as it is: negotiation is a skill
questions.recommendation: A. The cap itself is being fixed now as a contained bug; your answer sets the round limit.

questions.question: Should an empty, freshly built and decorated tank be able to sell at auction for more than its parts cost?
questions.why: The beauty multiplier and the 'Coherent, ethical display' bonus multiply the tank and equipment value, and empty tanks qualify. With normal buyer flow, a planted 40 gal tank with no animals nets roughly +20-25% after five days. The loop is repeatable and needs no livestock.
options: A: No: value the tank and equipment at depreciated cost; beauty raises only decor, plants and livestock; the display bonus needs animals
B: Keep the multipliers but require an established, stocked tank for the bonus
C: It's intended: aquascaping is a business; document and tune the margin
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: What is the minimum S3 automation that must ship, and what were 'options A and B' alongside ADR-0001's 'option C'?
questions.why: ADR-0001 says to push extended automation 'as far as safely coherent (option C)', but options A and B appear nowhere. The master lets the orchestrator simplify a single machine without an ADR, and only a 'substantial' cut needs one, so scope can shrink one step at a time.
options: A: All of Tiers 2-5 with the master's minimum concepts; simplifying any machine needs an ADR, a reviewer and your approval when a player would notice
B: Tiers 1, 2, 4 and 5 are mandatory; Tier 3 (feed production) is best effort
C: As written (the orchestrator's judgement, with an ADR only for substantial cuts)
questions.recommendation: A. Please also tell us what options A and B were, so the next ADR records option C verbatim.

questions.question: If the S3-D design arrives late or S3 gets blocked, may the Social stub and whole-stack hardening (S4) go ahead first?
questions.why: The design shipped production last and let it slip to 0.6. The master puts production and the not-yet-designed S3-D before S4, and ADR-0002 says S3 can't be accepted without S3-D, so a late design stops the whole program at an owner gate.
options: A: Keep the order and wait at the owner gate
B: Let S4 proceed while S3-D waits, then do S3-D plus a re-hardening pass before the Multiplayer Readiness Gate
C: Follow the design's order (Social before Production)
questions.recommendation: B.

questions.question: Who settles the production-line (S3-C) design gaps, and are these defaults right?
questions.why: You decided on several lines per species, but the approved design shows one line card with one route and test ids that can't tell lines apart. Its 'Never sell Prismatic' switch contradicts its own simulation (when off, a Prismatic would sit in quarantine forever). Its sell step lists 'Juveniles' after a quarantine most young outgrow, while the listing code rejects adults and caps active listings at 24.
options: A: Approve these defaults now: a list of line cards with a #/livestock/production/:lineId route and per-line test ids; lines may share grow-out and quarantine tanks but never a breeding pair or animal; a reserve price per line (default fair value −10%); automation never lists a Prismatic (the switch only chooses the safe tank); the listing type follows each animal's age at sale; when listing isn't possible, the batch waits in quarantine with a notice
B: Agents draft a production addendum through design intake for your approval before S3-C
C: You design it in Claude Design, like S3-D
questions.recommendation: B, with A's defaults as the draft.

questions.question: Should S3-D make water a tracked, limited resource?
questions.why: The master says automation must never create supplies from nothing, but today's Auto Top-Off and the designed Auto Water Changer use free freshwater (only salt is charged). Tracking water would change existing, approved behaviour.
options: A: Freshwater stays free; reserves track salt mix or prepared saltwater, and feed
B: All top-off and water-change water comes from tracked reservoirs with capacity and refills
C: Reservoirs are display only
questions.recommendation: A. Existing Auto Top-Off and Auto Water Changer behaviour stays unchanged unless the new devices are installed.

questions.question: How faithful must unwatched (background) tanks be to the tank you're looking at?
questions.why: Background tanks are simulated in 1-4 hour chunks. Moving animals between tanks skips or repeats up to about 4 game hours of their life, opening a far tank can rot a fresh meal, and short cool-water spawning cues vanish. S3's automation rules require results that don't depend on step size.
options: A: Strict: settle pending time before every action, move and focus change, and step at most 1 hour per chunk everywhere (more CPU on big facilities)
B: Settle pending time on every move, action and focus change; keep coarse chunks for idle tanks; record numeric tolerances and test them
C: Keep the current behaviour and document it
questions.recommendation: B, before S3.

questions.question: Should the 'notifications unsupported' message keep telling iPhone players to add the game to their Home Screen?
questions.why: The design's own risk list says iOS web notifications need a web-app manifest, which the game doesn't have, and a Home Screen copy would also start without the player's Safari save. Master §44 requires truthful copy.
options: A: Drop the sentence: 'This browser can't show notifications' / 'Alerts still appear in the game.'
B: Add a manifest and icons, test on a current iPhone, and warn that the Home Screen version keeps a separate save
C: Keep the copy
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: The approved Market notification promises 'auctions ending', but the game has no 'auction ending soon' event. Should we add one or change the wording?
questions.why: Only you can trade scope against approved copy. The event is useful, but it is new simulation work in the market code.
options: A: Add a deterministic event: once per listing, a few game hours before it ends, only when it has open bids, linking to the listing
B: Change the subtitle to 'New bids, sales and closed auctions'
C: B in 0.5, with A in the backlog
questions.recommendation: A, kept as narrow as described; fall back to C if S3 slips.

questions.question: Should developer tools ship in production builds?
questions.why: The production build includes window.__AQ (direct state edits, set game, add money, unlock all, make Prismatic, delete saves), a 'Developer tools' toggle in Settings, a ?dev=1 link parameter that turns dev mode on permanently, and ?fixture=…&autosave=1, which writes into the player's autosave. That's harmless in a single-player game, but any leaderboard value could be set from the console.
options: A: Keep everything as it is
B: Keep the Settings toggle; make ?dev=1 last only for the session; ignore fixture autosave in production; expose __AQ's write commands only in dev or QA builds, or with ?dev=1
C: Remove all developer tooling from production
questions.recommendation: B, before Social or leaderboards ship.

questions.question: How should the Social sign-in stub appear in a release build?
questions.why: The designed form accepts any email and any password of 8 or more characters and then says 'Signed in'. Browsers will offer to save the password for the shared GitHub Pages address, and the email is stored in localStorage. The 'prototype' hint shows only in dev mode.
options: A: As designed
B: A visible 'Preview: no real account' label, password autocomplete turned off, and no stored email (keeping the spec's fields and test ids)
C: Show Social only in dev builds until a backend exists
questions.recommendation: B (or C).

questions.question: What version should the eventual release carry, and what goes in 'What's new'?
questions.why: The design ships 0.5.0 with a fixed list that leaves out production lines and extended automation. The interim rule keeps the version at 0.4.0, with notes under '## Unreleased' (REL-003), until you approve a release plan.
options: A: One release, 0.5.0, with the list expanded
B: 0.5.0 for the designed scope, and 0.6.0 for production lines and extended automation
C: Decide at the final owner gate from prepared drafts
questions.recommendation: C.

questions.question: When you approve a release, should one approval cover both live sites, and should Render stay?
questions.why: render.yaml says autoDeploy: true, yet every Render deploy so far was triggered through its CLI. Pages and Render use different base paths. The owner package must list the exact remote actions.
options: A: Keep both; one approval covers both (same commit, checked through both version.json files)
B: Keep both, and approve each separately
C: Retire Render and keep GitHub Pages only
questions.recommendation: A, and at release make render.yaml's autoDeploy match reality (or fix the Render GitHub App's access).

questions.question: The GitHub repo is public. When you approve a push, should docs/agent be published with the code?
questions.why: docs/agent holds the master, the ADRs with your answers word for word, the design spec with the private canvas link, and the evidence. The harness is committed on the integration branch, so pushing that branch, or a main built from it, publishes all of it.
options: A: Publish the harness and evidence manifests; raw logs and transcripts stay ignored
B: Keep docs/agent and scripts/agent out of the public repo (push a release branch without them)
C: Publish a scrubbed copy
questions.recommendation: Decide before the first approved push: A if you're comfortable with it being public, otherwise B.

questions.question: Should the GitHub deploy workflow (and Render's build) run the unit tests before publishing?
questions.why: After an approved push nothing remote re-runs the test suite. Changing .github or render.yaml is something you'd see.
options: A: Yes: add npm test before the build (it takes effect only on a push you approve)
B: No: rely on the local gates and the owner package
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: What should 'deterministic' guarantee beyond today's definition?
questions.why: OPERATIONS §11, which an agent wrote, promises that the same state and the same sequence of calls give the same result on one device, and it accepts that the tank you watch, tick timing and autosave timing change outcomes (shop stock, money, Prismatic rolls). Multiplayer and a future notification forecast may need more.
options: A: Keep §11 as written; new S2 and S3 randomness uses keyed or per-subsystem streams
B: Also make saving neutral (save without first simulating pending time) and tie high-value rolls to the animal, so the tank you watch can't change them
C: Full replayability and identical results across browsers
questions.recommendation: A now; revisit at the Multiplayer Readiness Gate.

questions.question: Should market timers stay 'real time at any speed' during live play?
questions.why: Offers are promised in real minutes, so at 10× they last ten times as many game hours, and changing speed afterwards stretches or shrinks open deadlines. Offline catch-up now runs at 1× (fixed in the working tree).
options: A: Keep the real-time promises and re-base open deadlines when the speed changes
B: Make market timers pure game time
C: Keep them as they are
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: How price-sensitive should visitors be at high admission prices?
questions.why: Attendance never drops below 5%, so revenue keeps rising with price. The $40 slider limits players, but the simulation accepts up to $250.
options: A: Demand falls to near zero above about 2.5× the fair price, or visitors refuse tickets above their budget
B: Cap admission at a multiple of the fair price
C: Keep it as it is
questions.recommendation: A. The simulation's limit is being aligned with the $40 slider now.

questions.question: Should animals waiting in the holding container (after a tank sale or a save repair) be frozen in time?
questions.why: They currently don't eat, age or die, yet the game tells the player to give them a tank soon.
options: A: Explicit stasis, with honest wording
B: Simulate them like a small bare tank
C: Never strand animals: move them to a tank, or refuse the sale, at sale time
questions.recommendation: C where the sale can move them, with A as the fallback for save repair.

questions.question: Should players be able to move a tank after placing it?
questions.why: The simulation supports it and the room view has code for it, but no button has ever started it, and the S1 router will take over the field that code relies on.
options: A: Yes: add a Move action with its own UI state and a test
B: No: delete the unreachable UI code and keep placement final
C: Put it in the backlog
questions.recommendation: B now, and A later if you want rearranging.

questions.question: May the build add ESLint with the React hooks plugin as dev-only dependencies?
questions.why: The code has 46 suppression comments for a linter that isn't installed. Hook-dependency bugs, such as stale data in an open food picker, pass typecheck and tests. New dependencies need your approval.
options: A: Yes, dev-only, as a gate on src/ui from S1 (with an ADR)
B: No: review hook dependencies by hand
C: Decide after S1
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: Should tank status use one set of words everywhere ('Healthy / Watch / Danger', as design §18 says)?
questions.why: The same status reads 'Healthy', 'Good' or 'Act now' depending on where it appears.
options: A: Unify everywhere in S1
B: Keep 'Act now' as the Tanks list's call to action and unify the rest
C: Leave it as it is
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: If you pause while the welcome-back card is open, should closing it resume the old speed?
questions.why: Today closing the card overrides your pause, and saves made while the card is open store the old speed.
options: A: No: a speed change you make while the card is open wins
B: Yes (today's behaviour)
C: The card shouldn't pause the game at all
questions.recommendation: A. It is planned as a small fix unless you object.

questions.question: When Settings opens with no tab in the link, which tab should it show?
questions.why: Today Settings remembers the last tab, while design §20.4 says General is the default. S1's router needs one rule so that #/settings and #/settings/<tab> behave predictably.
options: A: Always General; links choose a tab, and the URL follows tab clicks
B: The last tab used this session, shown in the URL
C: Today's behaviour (the URL ignores tabs)
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: Should per-frame AI code ever change saved game state?
questions.why: Exactly one AI path does today: TankAI's 'observed' hook advances tutorial steps, which can pay rewards. The revised AGENTS.md allows 'AI actions' through mutate without limits, while ARCHITECTURE.md says the AI writes only to runtime data.
options: A: Only the existing tutorial 'observed:*' flags, documented as the single exception; anything else needs an ADR
B: Never: route observations through the UI or the game loop (a small refactor)
C: Allow AI actions broadly
questions.recommendation: A.

questions.question: Which model context window should the harness budget for?

synthesis.themes:
Fifteen reviewers produced 173 findings that survived verification. They merge into 101 issues: 2 high, 37 medium, 58 low and 4 informational. There are 57 deduplicated owner questions; 6 of them block the build. Questions the owner already answered in ADR-0002 (where harness commits go, the session model and relaunch, who designs S3-D, what to do with game bugs) were dropped.

1. Strong constitution, weak mechanics. As committed (94de6bb), the owner's harness asked for things Claude Code can't do as written: a fresh context after every slice together with automatic advance. Its state flow used a state missing from the list of legal states. It never defined how an approval is recorded. Repair attempts counted only when the repairer judged them 'materially different'. The ban on remote actions was prose only. The uncommitted S0 revision (ADR-0003: OPERATIONS.md, scripts/agent with tests, schema-2 STATE and REQUIREMENTS, a design registry and intake procedure, and a reconciled master) already closes most of the 64 harness findings. What remains is wiring and verification:
- BACKLOG.md, PROTECTED.json, ADR-0004 and evidence/S0/reviews are referenced but don't exist yet.
- check-state doesn't tie reviews or browser runs to the reviewed code.
- check-state accepts NOT_APPLICABLE on any gate and requires only 6 of the 11 gate keys.
- The append-only checks compare only against HEAD.
- protect.mjs accepts any ADR as approval.
- The registry decomposition (S0-T6) isn't finished.

2. Authority and self-reference. Files an agent writes can stand in for owner authority: STATE flags, ADRs marked 'Accepted', and protect.mjs --update. S0 also builds the checkers that will judge S0. ADR-0003 itself is marked Accepted on the strength of a general 'improve it'. Ratifying it at S0-T12 is the pivotal owner decision. Mechanical push and deploy guards are the only controls that don't depend on agent-written files, and only the owner may install them.

3. Evidence has to be bound to the code it judged. Gates could pass against a foreign server or against stale or ignored logs. Command gates are now bound to the code tree; reviews and browser runs are not yet. Headless Chromium can't start in the sandbox (BF-001), so e2e and browser QA have no lawful path to GREEN until the owner decides how browser work runs.

4. The written rules don't match the code. The single-mutate-path rule, the simRng-only rule and 'rendering never writes' misdescribe the code. About fifteen statements in the approved design are wrong about today's code (router targets, toast placement, genetics visibility, notification sources, verdict labels). They need one errata path, applied through slice contracts rather than silent edits.

5. Time and determinism ahead of S3. Live play isn't replayable by design (now documented in OPERATIONS §11). The real risks:
- A tick that throws used to commit half a step. This is fixed in the tree; the freeze UX is still open.
- Moving animals between tanks ignores pending simulation time.
- Coarse background chunks lose events that happen inside a chunk.
- A second RNG inside a tank step forks the main stream.
S3's automation promises (atomic, idempotent, independent of step size, never runs twice) depend on all four.

6. Players' data. A future schema bump could let the deployed v0.4.0 code overwrite newer saves; this is high severity and needs an owner policy. Crafted saves are hardened in the tree. Exit paths (load, return to title, reload, crash) can drop unsaved play.

7. Economy loops: the counter-offer ratchet, profitable empty-tank flips, and quick-sale counter inflation all pass the current tests. S3's auto-listing would amplify them.

8. Already fixed in the uncommitted working tree, and each needs committing plus an independent review:
- atomic mutateFast
- the hidden-tab catch-up overlap
- offline market at 1×
- equipment staying intact during the offline grace
- locale-independent state
- crafted-save keys and listing photos
- gate configuration (E2E_REUSE, requireAssertions, forbidOnly, e2e typecheck)
- .gitignore

Conventions used here:
- fix-now-harness covers docs/agent, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and scripts/agent. All of these are protected under OPERATIONS §10: the constitution and prompts change only through an owner-approved ADR, and scripts through an ADR plus a reviewer's sign-off.
- fix-now-app-safe follows ADR-0002 decision 2: a contained fix with a test and an independent review.
- Each entry's severity is the highest verifier-corrected severity among the findings merged into it. The summaries say what the working tree already fixes.
