findings.title: Unattended relaunch sessions keep remote-capable channels that the Bash-only deny list and the reflog check never see
findings.evidence: relaunch.mjs:16-18: 'Sessions run with --permission-mode auto and --permission-prompts none ... plus deny rules ... Deny rules match the command text, so they are a guard rail rather than a guarantee; the post-session push and remote checks back them up.' Every DENY_RULES entry (:33-69) is a Bash(...) prefix. claudeArgs (:171-192) passes no --strict-mcp-config, --tools or --disallowedTools. The child is spawned with env: { ...process.env, ... } (:240). The only push detector counts 'update by push' reflog lines (:117-126), and REL-001's measurable criterion is exactly that (REQUIREMENTS.json:52). ADR-0003:100-101 relies on it: 'The relaunch launcher applies deny rules to the sessions it starts.' KICKOFF.md:14 says to run it 'from a terminal in the repo'. On this machine those are CNVS terminals. This session's environment has PATH starting with /Applications/CNVS.app/Contents/MacOS (which holds cnvsctl) and exports CNVSCTL, CNVS_CONTROL_URL and CNVS_CONTROL_TOKEN. `cnvsctl --help` lists 'run-shell [--target VALUE] --command VALUE', 'spawn-agent [--agent VALUE] ... [--prompt VALUE] ... [--headless]' and 'git --kind VALUE'. The CNVS MCP tool cnvs_git is described as 'Run a git action (save, status, push, ...)'. The same Claude Code install also gives this review session RemoteTrigger ('create: POST /v1/code/triggers', 'run'), CronCreate, Artifact publishing and claude.ai Docs connector tools. OPERATIONS.md:62 forbids publishing 'to any external service (including gists and artifacts)'. `claude --help` (2.1.289) says that under -p 'The workspace trust dialog is skipped' and 'Settings files that fail validation are silently ignored in this mode'. Nothing in scripts/agent looks for a new .claude/settings*.json, hook or .mcp.json (rg '\.claude|\.mcp\.json' scripts/agent finds nothing). OPERATIONS.md:210-211 says gh 'isn't on the agent shell's PATH', but here /opt/homebrew/bin is on PATH and `which gh` resolves to ~/.local/bin/gh (-> /Volumes/Dev/Developer/tools/bin/gh). So the '!gh auth git-credential' helper in .git/config would authenticate a push without prompting. The Bash-text bypasses, URL and tag pushes and the editable settings file are already in evidence/S0/reviews/code-architecture-harness-1.md M9 and aren't repeated here.
findings.harnessRule: Nothing leaves this machine without the owner's explicit yes (AGENTS.md; OPERATIONS §3, including artifacts). ADR-0003: the launcher's deny rules enforce this for unattended sessions. REL-001.
findings.impact: An unattended session could push to main (which deploys Pages), deploy, publish, or start unrestricted agents through channels the launcher neither blocks nor detects. Examples: `cnvsctl run-shell --command 'git push origin HEAD:main'` runs in a CNVS terminal outside Claude's permission checks. A RemoteTrigger routine runs in the cloud. A SessionStart hook that one session writes into .claude/settings.json runs unprompted in the next headless session. The reflog check comes after the fact and can't undo a deploy, and REL-001 stays GREEN.
findings.fix: Do this before any unattended run (relaunch.mjs is protected, so it needs an ADR and a security-data review). (1) Spawn the child with an env allowlist: drop CNVS*, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_*, GH_*/GITHUB_*, RENDER_* and VERCEL_*, and take the CNVS dir off PATH. (2) Pass --strict-mcp-config and an explicit --tools or --disallowedTools list that excludes RemoteTrigger, CronCreate/CronDelete, Artifact*, SendMessage and the mcp__ connectors. (3) Block pushes below Claude: set GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE with remote.origin.pushurl set to an invalid URL and credential.helper set to empty, plus GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and an empty GH_CONFIG_DIR. (4) After each session, compare a read-only `git ls-remote origin` with its pre-session value, raise an alarm on new .claude/, .mcp.json or hook files, and record `claude --version`. (5) Name these channels in OPERATIONS §3 and REL-001.

votes.reason: The core claim holds. The launcher's only enforcement is a list of Bash(...) text deny rules. It hands the child its full environment and passes no tool or MCP restrictions, and on this machine there are working remote paths that those rules never name. Several details are overstated, though. (a) A `git push origin HEAD:main` sent through `cnvsctl run-shell` runs against the same .git, so it still writes an "update by push" entry to the refs/remotes/origin/main reflog. relaunch.mjs:89 would raise an alarm and REL-001 would not "stay GREEN". It is caught only after the fact, after Pages has deployed. Pushes the reflog really misses are URL or tag pushes and cloud RemoteTrigger routines. (b) The CNVS MCP tools (cnvs_git and the rest) reach this review session through `--mcp-config <CNVS terminal dir>/mcp-config.json` on its own command line, which the parent process shows. A child started with relaunch.mjs's argv does not get that flag. The live CNVS route for the child is Bash `cnvsctl`, which is on PATH and authenticated by the inherited CNVS_CONTROL_TOKEN and related variables, not the MCP tool. (c) Under --permission-mode auto, the Bash call to cnvsctl itself still goes through Claude's auto-mode check. Only the command it dispatches runs outside Claude, so "outside Claude's permission checks" is only half true. (d) Two framing details are stale: HEAD is c774d38, not 0d9fc5a, and docs/agent is now tracked except for ADR-0004/0005 and S0/reviews. Taken together this is real defense-in-depth debt in an opt-in launcher. It needs the agent to break its explicit instructions (UNATTENDED_NOTE: "a denied action stays denied: do not retry it another way. Never push, deploy, publish"), so medium fits better than high.
votes.fixAssessment: The direction is right, and steps (1), (2), (4) and (5) are sound, but three corrections are needed. (i) In step (3), `credential.helper=` set through GIT_CONFIG_* clears only the generic helper list. The URL-scoped `credential.https://github.com.helper` (which runs /opt/homebrew/bin/gh) is a different key and would still authenticate, so it has to be emptied too, or use `credential.useHttpPath`, or better, set `remote.origin.pushurl` to an invalid value and also `url.invalid://.insteadOf=https://github.com/` for push. (ii) Step (3) only reaches processes that inherit the child's environment. A push dispatched via `cnvsctl run-shell` runs in a CNVS terminal with CNVS's own environment, so for that channel step (1) is the real control: strip every CNVS* variable, remove /Applications/CNVS.app/Contents/MacOS from PATH, and also add 'Bash(cnvsctl *)' and 'Bash(*/cnvsctl *)' to DENY_RULES. Also check that cnvsctl can't find its control endpoint without the environment, for example from a file under ~/Library/Application Support/CNVS. (iii) For step (2), it is simpler and stronger to start the child with `--strict-mcp-config` (with no --mcp-config) plus an explicit `--tools Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep,...` allowlist instead of a disallow list. Also consider `--setting-sources user` or `--restricted`-style handling so that a .claude/settings.json or hook written by one session doesn't load in the next. Step (4)'s `git ls-remote origin` is a read-only network call, which is acceptable, and it catches URL and tag pushes that the reflog misses. Also fix OPERATIONS.md:210-211: gh is on PATH, and the github.com credential helper calls it by absolute path. relaunch.mjs, OPERATIONS and REQUIREMENTS are protected files, so these changes need an ADR and owner approval, as the finding says.

votes.reason:
The core claim holds. relaunch.mjs only blocks Bash command text and only detects pushes through the reflog. It passes the child the parent's whole environment and puts no limits on tools or MCP servers. So remote-capable channels outside Bash(git push|gh|render|vercel) stay open, and neither the launcher nor REL-001 mentions them.

The finding overstates two things:
(a) The cnvs MCP tools (cnvs_git, cnvs_run_shell, cnvs_spawn_agent) would NOT be loaded in a relaunch child. CNVS starts its own claude processes with an explicit `--mcp-config <per-terminal mcp-config.json> --settings <per-terminal claude-settings.json>` (seen in ps). ~/.claude.json has no user-level or project-level mcpServers. A plain `claude -p` spawned by relaunch.mjs gets neither. What does reach the child is the cnvsctl CLI through Bash, because PATH and CNVS_CONTROL_URL/TOKEN are inherited. The child also gets the account-level claude.ai connectors, plugin MCP servers and the built-in RemoteTrigger, CronCreate and Artifact tools.
(b) The child runs in --permission-mode auto, so the auto-mode classifier still checks every Bash and MCP call. A command like `cnvsctl run-shell --command 'git push origin HEAD:main'` still has the push in its text. A careless push is therefore unlikely; the realistic case is a session deliberately working around UNATTENDED_NOTE ("a denied action stays denied: do not retry it another way").

Other things that lower the practical impact: relaunch is opt-in and has never been run for real (the dry run in code-architecture-harness-1 refused to start because check-state reports errors). In ADR-0004 the owner chose "text rules only" for now.

Much of the proposed fix repeats findings already on record. security-data-1.md SD-4 covers credential stripping through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, GH_CONFIG_DIR and `git ls-remote`. SD-5 covers `.claude/settings*.json`, `.mcp.json` and hooks loading without a trust prompt under -p, plus the editable settings file. What this finding adds is the non-Bash channels (the cnvsctl env/PATH, claude.ai connectors, RemoteTrigger/Cron/Artifact, messaging-socket env) and a false statement in OPERATIONS. Severity: medium, not high.
votes.fixAssessment:
The direction is right and safe, since the changes only shrink what the child can reach. relaunch.mjs and REL-001 are protected, so the fix needs an ADR and the owner's yes. Tie it to the existing SD-4/SD-5 fixes rather than opening a separate track.

Refinements:
(1) Use an env allowlist, not a denylist. Pass HOME, USER, LANG, TMPDIR, PATH and the Claude auth variables. Rebuild PATH without the CNVS.app directory. Explicitly drop CNVS_*, CNVSCTL, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_*, GH_*/GITHUB_*, RENDER_*, VERCEL_* and SSH_AUTH_SOCK.
(2) Pass `--strict-mcp-config` with an empty `--mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`. votes.reason:

It hands the child the full parent env, including the CNVS control credentials and cnvsctl on PATH. Its only push detector is the "update by push" reflog. REL-001 and ADR-0003 rely on this launcher as the unattended guard.

I am lowering the severity from high to medium, for four reasons:
(a) The launcher is opt-in and has never run: the ledger has 0 events with actor "relaunch". The owner's next sessions are planned in the Claude desktop app (ADR-0004 decision 2).
(b) The script header says openly that the deny rules are "a guard rail rather than a guarantee". The owner chose "text rules only, for now" for mechanical guards (ADR-0004 decision 1, verbatim "lets not worry about this for now maybe 3 then").
(c) Sessions run under --permission-mode auto plus --permission-prompts none, which the finding ignores. That is another layer: anything that would prompt is denied. I could not test without running a headless session, so it remains possible that RemoteTrigger, Artifact or a cnvsctl push actually gets through.
(d) A `git push origin HEAD:main` run through a CNVS terminal in this same repo would still write the remote-tracking reflog and trigger the alarm, though only after the deploy.

What is new: the CNVS channel inherited through the env and PATH, the cloud and connector tools (RemoteTrigger, Cron, Artifact, claude.ai Docs, the Vercel plugin), the missing --tools/--disallowedTools/--strict-mcp-config flags, and the stale OPERATIONS statement that gh is not on PATH.

Note: the actual HEAD is c774d38 on agent/aquariumgo-local-stack-20261005, not 0d9fc5a. The cited lines match anyway.
votes.fixAssessment:
The direction is right, but parts of the fix as written are wrong or would break things. relaunch.mjs is protected, and the owner deferred mechanical guards, so the minimal safe step now is an owner question. The fix should also become a precondition in OPERATIONS/REL-001: "don't run relaunch.mjs unattended until X". Agents should not implement it on their own.

Specific corrections:

**(1) Env allowlist**
- A strict allowlist risks dropping vars sessions need: HOME, TMPDIR, PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, E2E_PORT and the auth or keychain context.
- Use a denylist instead. Delete keys matching ^(CNVS|CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_|GH_|GITHUB_|RENDER_|VERCEL_|NETLIFY_) plus SSH_AUTH_SOCK.
- Filter the CNVS.app directory out of PATH.
- This is the only part that closes the cnvsctl route. Without CNVS_CONTROL_TOKEN/URL, cnvsctl can't reach the control server.
- Simpler still: have preflight refuse to start while CNVSCTL or CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET is set, and tell the owner to run it from a plain Terminal.app.

**(2) Tool restrictions**
- An explicit --tools allowlist would break the harness unless it includes Agent/Task. CLAUDE.md requires the reviewer roles to run as separate subagents.
- It must also keep WebFetch/WebSearch, because OPERATIONS §3 allows read-only research.
- Prefer --disallowedTools for: RemoteTrigger, CronCreate, CronDelete, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, SendMessage, PushNotification, DesignSync, mcp__claude_ai_*, mcp__cnvs__* and mcp__plugin_vercel_*.
- Add --strict-mcp-config with no --mcp-config.
- Consider --setting-sources project,local, so that user-enabled plugins like the Vercel one, with its deploy skill, don't load. The orchestrator would have to check that this keeps authentication working.

**(3) Git credentials and push URL**

- GIT_CONFIG_* only reaches child processes. It does nothing for a command run in a CNVS terminal, so (1) is the load-bearing part.

**(4) and (5)**

**Tests:** none of this changes decide() or preflight() semantics except an optional new preflight refusal. agent.test.mjs relaunch tests should keep passing, with a new test added for any new preflight problem.

findings.title: Gate evidence records the code tree from before the run, so a gate that ran while the tree was being edited still counts as passing
findings.evidence: evidence.mjs:99-101 computes head, dirty and `const codeTree = codeTreeOf(null)` before `spawn(command, ...)` at :104-108. The record at :113-129 stores that pre-run tree, and nothing recomputes it after exit. check-state.mjs:126-128 accepts a GREEN gate when rec.codeTree equals the current or checkpoint tree. OPERATIONS.md:160-162 says 'A gate result is valid only for the tree it ran on'. OPERATIONS.md:24-25 lets a session keep working while 'long background work' runs. OPERATIONS.md:208-209 and the S0 manifest show gates running for minutes: typecheck 223 s, build 544 s, e2e 718 s. No rule or lock stops builders, background agents or the owner from editing the shared working tree during a run; master §3.4 only says 'Reviewers may use additional local worktrees'.
findings.harnessRule: OPERATIONS §6: 'A gate result is valid only for the tree it ran on'. Master §28 evidence rules.
findings.impact: Suppose a unit, build or e2e run starts on tree A and picks up an edit made a minute later (or the edit is reverted before the next record). It is still recorded as passing on A. At the checkpoint, check-state then certifies A even though the files that passed were never exactly A.
findings.fix: Recompute the tree after the command exits and mark the record invalid (treeChanged) when it differs. Better: run each gate in a throwaway worktree checked out from a snapshot commit of the exact tree. State in OPERATIONS §6 that a gate's tree is frozen while it runs.

votes.reason: The finding holds. In the committed scripts/agent/evidence.mjs, runAndRecord computes `const codeTree = codeTreeOf(null)` at line 101, before `spawn(command, ...)` at line 105, and stores that value in the record. Nothing in the committed code recomputes it after the run. check-state.mjs:126-128 accepts a GREEN gate whenever rec.codeTree matches the tree it is checking against. OPERATIONS.md:161 says "A gate result is valid only for the tree it ran on", but no rule in OPERATIONS or the master freezes the tree while a gate runs (a grep for "frozen" finds nothing). The S0 manifest confirms the long runs on a dirty shared tree: typecheck 223 s, unit 101 s, build 544 s, e2e 718 s, all on tree 454801df with dirty=true. A partial fix is already in progress: the uncommitted evidence.mjs now records codeTreeAfter and treeChanged at lines 149-150. Nothing reads that flag yet, so the hole is still open (details in fixAssessment).
votes.fixAssessment: The proposed fix is right in direction but incomplete as written, and the uncommitted partial fix is incomplete in the same way. (1) Recording treeChanged does nothing on its own. validateGateEvidence in check-state.mjs (around line 125) must treat `rec.treeChanged` like a failed run: an error at acceptance and a warning otherwise. verify-slice.mjs:43 should count such a run as failed (or at least not passed) and print the reason. (2) Comparing the tree after the run cannot catch an edit that is reverted before the command exits (A to B to A); the finding names this case itself. Closing it needs isolation: snapshot the exact tree (for example `git stash create`, or a commit of a throwaway index from codeTreeOf), check it out with `git worktree add --detach` under /Volumes/Dev, symlink node_modules, give it its own E2E_PORT, run the gate there, and record the snapshot's tree. (3) Add a rule to OPERATIONS §6 and the checkpoint procedure step 1: until gates run in isolation, nobody (builders, background agents, the owner) edits code or config in the shared working tree while a gate is running. The cheap fix (flag plus check-state rejection plus the rule) is safe and should land now. Running gates in a worktree is the stronger follow-up, but it touches e2e port and node_modules handling, so it needs care.

votes.reason:
The gap is real, but it matters much less than "medium" suggests. In committed HEAD (c774d38; the finding's 0d9fc5a is origin/main), runAndRecord takes codeTreeOf(null) before the spawn and never checks it again. The uncommitted working-tree evidence.mjs has already started a fix: it now recomputes the tree after exit and adds {codeTreeAfter, treeChanged:true}. Nothing reads that flag yet. verify-slice.mjs still sets gates[gate]='GREEN' on exit 0, and check-state.mjs (unchanged from HEAD) compares only rec.codeTree. The tree is also not frozen during a run. No rule stops concurrent edits (master §3.4 only says reviewers "may" use worktrees), and nothing locks the tree. So the hole exists.

What lowers the impact: at acceptance, check-state errors when rec.codeTree differs from the checkpoint commit's tree. If an edit made during a run is kept, the checkpoint tree differs from the recorded pre-run tree and the check catches it. The only case that gets through is a mixed-state run: an edit made during the run and reverted to exactly tree A before the checkpoint. Even then, all gates must be re-run on the final tree before the checkpoint (OPERATIONS checkpoint step 1). It needs a concurrent writer in the shared tree during a minutes-long gate, plus an exact revert. Reviewers are read-only. Nothing touches player saves or the game. It is a harness-integrity gap that is rare and needs several things to line up, so low.
votes.fixAssessment:
Recomputing the tree after exit is right and safe, and it is half done in the working tree. To finish it:
1. In verify-slice.mjs, set the gate to RED (or leave it unset) when rec.treeChanged, and print why.
2. In validateGateEvidence (check-state.mjs), treat `rec.treeChanged` as an error for a GREEN gate.
3. Add a test in agent.test.mjs for both.
4. State in OPERATIONS §6 that nobody edits the shared tree while a gate runs.

The before/after check cannot detect an edit that is made and then reverted within one run. Only the stronger option closes that: run each gate in a throwaway worktree or checkout of a snapshot commit, or at least take a lock file that builders must respect. That option costs more, because each worktree needs its own node_modules and E2E_PORT, so it is a reasonable later step. The recorded flag plus enforcement is a sufficient fix at this severity.

That included '[Render manual deploy](render-manual-deploy.md) — OWNER-ONLY: ... Render CLI command inside'. gh-cli-path.md's front matter has 'originSessionId: 588d9af1-60a1-4863-b141-33e248e04e00' (the session on every S0 LEDGER.jsonl event) and 'modified: 2026-10-05T19:08:46.192Z'. render-manual-deploy.md was modified at 2026-10-05T19:08:44Z. findings.harnessRule: Master §0 and §14 (no hidden model memory is authoritative; context firewall). AGENTS.md: 'The repository is the memory.' OPERATIONS §7: reviewer independence.
findings.impact: Any session, unattended ones included, can leave lasting instructions or verdict hints (for example 'finding X is accepted') that every later orchestrator and every reviewer reads, outside the protected and reviewed files. Builder, reviewer and orchestrator events all carry the same session id, so reviewer independence can't be shown from the ledger.
findings.fix: Owner policy (see the questions): either agents don't write auto-memory for this project, or auto-memory is off for harness sessions. check-state warns when the memory directory's hash changes. Move the Render auto-deploy fact into OPERATIONS §3. Record the reviewer's agent id or a transcript hash in each review record instead of relying on the session id.

votes.reason: The core facts check out. Claude Code injects the project auto-memory into every session, subagents included; it appears in this verifier's own context. The current harness session (588d9af1) edited that memory today. Every LEDGER.jsonl event carries that one session id. A spawned subagent has the same CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, with CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1. So the ledger can't tell a reviewer from the orchestrator, and OPERATIONS §7's claim that a reviewer 'receives only what its prompt lists' is not literally true: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and MEMORY.md are always injected. Several details are overstated, though. (1) The master already covers the authority question. Line 23 says auto-memory is 'hints, they never authorise anything, and docs/agent wins any conflict', and AGENTS.md:13-15 says the same. The remaining gap is a missing write rule and missing detection, not a missing rule on authority. (2) The memory content I found agrees with the harness: both files say to push or deploy only on Brian's explicit yes in the current session. The 'verdict hints' injection the finding describes is hypothetical. (3) Reviewers don't write ledger events (§7: the orchestrator records the reports), so 'reviewer events carry the same session id' is imprecise. The real point is that the ledger holds no evidence of reviewer independence. (4) The claim that the Render autoDeploy fact 'appears nowhere in docs/agent' is not quite right. render.yaml:9 has `autoDeploy: true`, OPERATIONS.md:60-61 documents CLI/API-triggered Render deploys, and the S0 security-data-1.md review (SD-12) already flags the autoDeploy/OPERATIONS mismatch. Only the observation 'no commit-triggered deploy has ever run' is found only in memory. (5) The lib.mjs line numbers are right for HEAD (c774d38, not 0d9fc5a as the task states). The working-tree copy is modified and has the code at lines 245/302. The bootstrap-check lines are 60-61. Because the rule on authority already exists and the observed content is benign, I'm downgrading this to low.
votes.fixAssessment: The fix is mostly right and safe, and it is properly an owner decision. Changes: (a) Add a rule to AGENTS.md and the master that agents don't write or edit project auto-memory during harness runs, or write only tool-path hints, never state, verdicts or instructions. A check-state warning keyed to a hash of the memory directory is a reasonable alarm, but it reads a file outside the repo, so it must be advisory only and must tolerate a missing directory. (b) Record the Render observation ('autoDeploy is declared, but every deploy so far was triggered by the API') in OPERATIONS §3 alongside the existing SD-12 fix, rather than as a new standalone item. (c) Correct OPERATIONS §7 to say that harness-injected context (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, auto-memory) also reaches reviewers, so 'only what its prompt lists' means only what the orchestrator passes on. (d) For independence, don't rely on CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID: subagents inherit it. Have the review record carry the subagent or agent id and a hash of the exact prompt given to the reviewer, so a later check can confirm the prompt left out HANDOFF, the LEDGER and builder narrative. Keep the bootstrap freshness check on session id; there a shared id fails safe, since a child of the closing session is rejected.

votes.reason:
The memory-channel half holds up. Auto-memory is injected into every session, subagents included: this verifier's own context opens with the MEMORY.md index. The harness says memory is non-authoritative but nothing forbids writing to it, nothing watches it, and the reviewer prompts never tell reviewers to ignore it. So OPERATIONS §7's claim that a reviewer "receives only what its prompt lists" is not literally true. Even so, the impact is smaller than claimed and the severity is overstated:
(1) The harness already says four times that memory carries no authority: master §0 line 23 ("they are hints, they never authorise anything, and `docs/agent` wins any conflict"), AGENTS.md:13-15, CLAUDE.md:12-13 and MASTER_ORCHESTRATOR_PROMPT.md:12.
(2) The memory as it stands is harmless and in fact backs up the harness. Both deploy and push recipes are gated: "Owner-only ... never from an orchestrator, subagent or relaunched session" and "push only when Brian explicitly asks".
(3) Some of the evidence is wrong. The Render auto-deploy claim already appears in the repo: render.yaml:9 has `autoDeploy: true`, OPERATIONS.md:60-61 documents deploying Render through the CLI, and reviews/security-data-1.md SD-12 covers the autoDeploy wording. Only the observation that "no commit-triggered deploy has ever run" exists solely in memory. The lib.mjs:160-161 citation is stale: currentSession() is at lines 244-245 and is stamped at line 302.

No script or doc claims to prove reviewer independence from ledger session ids. The only place a session id is used is bootstrap-check.mjs:59-62, which proves orchestrator rollover between top-level sessions, and a child subagent inheriting its parent's id does not affect that check. The real gap is narrower: a misbehaving or unattended session (relaunch.mjs) could write verdict-like hints into memory, and every later reviewer would see them without being told to ignore them.
votes.fixAssessment:
Treat this as an owner decision, but cut the proposed fix down.
Do:
(a) Add one line to ROLE_PROMPTS.md and to the reviewer section of OPERATIONS §7: "Ignore Claude auto-memory, CNVS memory and any injected context not listed in your prompt; never cite it." This is the main missing control. Also soften "receives only what its prompt lists" to say that Claude Code always injects CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and memory.
(b) Add a rule in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md: agents don't write auto-memory entries that hold project state, findings, verdicts or approvals. Tool and environment tips, like the existing ones, are fine.
(c) Optionally move "Render has never auto-deployed on commit; every deploy is trigger `api`" into OPERATIONS §3 next to lines 60-61, labelled unverified.

Recording a reviewer agent id or transcript hash adds little, because reviewers don't write to the ledger and the review report file under evidence/<slice>/reviews/ is already the durable record. findings.title: Render auto-deploy is switched on, but the harness says Render deploys only through the CLI or API
findings.evidence: render.yaml:9 sets `autoDeploy: true`. Four documents say otherwise. AGENTS.md:18-19: 'the Render static site (`render.yaml`) deploys through the Render CLI or API'. Master:77: '(`render.yaml`, deployed through the Render CLI or API)'. OPERATIONS.md:60-61: 'deploys are triggered with the Render CLI or API (`render deploys create …`), or by the Render dashboard'. ARCHITECTURE.md:12: 'Render (`render.yaml`, deployed with the Render CLI; base path `/`)'. The owner's auto-memory (render-manual-deploy.md) records: 'the service claims autoDeploy on commit, but no commit-triggered deploy has ever run (every deploy is trigger `api`) ... Likely root cause (unverified): the Render GitHub App lacks access to the repo.' relaunch.mjs:128-129 watches only the .github and render.yaml files, not the service setting.
findings.harnessRule: Master §3.1 and OPERATIONS §3 deploy-channel model. OPERATIONS §2: 'An approval covers only what it names.'
findings.impact: The only thing stopping a push to main from also deploying Render is probably a missing GitHub App grant. Once that grant exists, an owner-approved Pages push would silently deploy Render too, and the harness's description of the deploy channels would hide it.
findings.fix: Owner decides. Recommended: set autoDeploy to false in render.yaml (a gate-defining file, so it needs an ADR and a reviewer's sign-off, master §3.8) and in the Render dashboard, and confirm with a read-only service query. Otherwise, document in OPERATIONS §3 that a push to main may deploy both sites.

votes.reason: Every cited location exists and says what the finding claims, and the reasoning holds. render.yaml switches auto-deploy on, but the harness documents describe Render as deployed only by the CLI, the API or the dashboard. Neither the harness nor the scripts say that a push to main could also deploy Render. The owner's memory is the only source for the claim that commit-triggered deploys never run, and it gives the likely cause as unverified. So whether Render deploys on push depends on an outside setting that the harness neither records nor checks. I lowered the severity to low for three reasons. Nothing can happen unless the owner first approves a push to main, which is already gated. Render would serve the same commit the owner approved for Pages. And the hazard needs a GitHub App grant that does not exist today. Two small corrections: the real HEAD is c774d38, not 0d9fc5a. An existing S0 review (security-data-1.md SD-12) already flags the same autoDeploy wording problem, so this finding partly duplicates it.
votes.fixAssessment: Leaving the decision to the owner is the right call. The cheapest safe fix needs no remote action: edit OPERATIONS §3 (and the matching lines in AGENTS.md:18-19, master:77 and ARCHITECTURE.md:12) to say that Render has auto-deploy on (render.yaml:9 and the service setting). They should also say commit-triggered deploys have not run so far, probably because of a missing GitHub App grant. Then approving a push to main must be treated as possibly deploying both sites, and the approval ADR should name both. That keeps OPERATIONS §2 ("An approval covers only what it names") true. The finding's preferred fix is to set autoDeploy to false in render.yaml and in the dashboard. That fix works, but it has costs the finding understates. The dashboard toggle is a change to remote settings, which OPERATIONS §3 forbids without the owner's recorded approval. Changing render.yaml only affects the service if the service is synced from the Blueprint, so a read-only service query (for example `render services` / GET service autoDeploy) has to come first. And editing render.yaml stops the launcher for review, as the finding notes. Either way, the memory index line "Render never auto-deploys on push" should be reworded, because it states as fact something the memory itself marks unverified. This finding should be merged with SD-12 so it is not reported twice.

votes.reason:
The mismatch is real, but the impact is overstated, so I'd lower it from medium to low. render.yaml:9 says `autoDeploy: true`. AGENTS.md:18-19, master:77, OPERATIONS.md:59-60 and ARCHITECTURE.md:12 all say Render deploys through the CLI, API or dashboard. None of them mentions that a push might also trigger a Render deploy.

How it could happen: Render would deploy on a commit to main only if the Blueprint or dashboard setting is in force and the Render GitHub App can see the repo. That chain starts with a push to main, and every one of the harness docs already forbids that without the owner's verbatim, ADR-recorded yes. An autonomous agent following the harness therefore can't reach this path on its own.

What it costs if it happens: the owner has approved a push to main, and Render rebuilds from that same commit. The owner's own runbook (memory/render-manual-deploy.md) already says to run `render deploys create ... --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)` straight after every approved push. So the "silent" extra deploy would ship the build the owner was about to deploy by hand anyway. It doesn't touch players' saves or the simulation. The real harm is narrow: the deploy-channel docs are inaccurate, and approval scope is fuzzy for a push the owner wanted on Pages only.

Two parts of the finding are speculative. The "missing GitHub App grant" is the only claimed blocker, and the memory file itself calls that cause "unverified". It also says no commit-triggered deploy has ever run.

This is also a duplicate. docs/agent/evidence/S0/reviews/security-data-1.md SD-12 (line 214 onward) already flags the same `autoDeploy: true` vs OPERATIONS §3 wording at Low severity, with the fix "say 'a push to main may deploy both channels'".
votes.fixAssessment:
The proposed fix works but is heavier than it needs to be.

The safe, immediate fix is the documentation option, which matches SD-12. Edit OPERATIONS §3, the master §3.1 line, AGENTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md to say: "render.yaml declares autoDeploy: true. Commit-triggered Render deploys haven't been seen so far, but a push to main may deploy both channels. Treat any push approval as covering both unless the owner says otherwise." These are harness docs, not gate-defining code, and they make the approval scope honest whatever the Render settings are.

Flipping `autoDeploy` to false in render.yaml is the owner's call. On its own it may change nothing: the YAML only applies if the service is Blueprint-managed and synced, and the live setting is the dashboard or service setting. Changing that live setting is a remote configuration write, which OPERATIONS §3 forbids without recorded approval, so only the owner can do it. Render's current Blueprint field is `autoDeployTrigger` (commit/off/checksPass); `autoDeploy` is the legacy boolean. Anyone changing it should use the current field.

A read-only check is allowed and worth doing first, because it settles whether the risk exists at all: `render services list -o json`, or a GET on the service, to read its autoDeploy/trigger and repo-link state.

Fold this finding into SD-12 rather than tracking it separately.

findings.title: The GitHub repo is public, and nothing decides which parts of docs/agent may be published: logs, reviews, the owner's words and write-ups of live-site flaws
findings.evidence: I ran a read-only anonymous check with credentials disabled: `git -c credential.helper= ls-remote --heads https://github.com/GrayGrayson1/aquarium-go.git` returned `0d9fc5a46085f746510a1041335632cd4f7314a2 refs/heads/main`, so the repo is public. The owner's gh-cli-path.md memory also says 'public'. .gitignore:17-18 force-commits evidence logs ('!docs/agent/evidence/**/*.log'). Reviewer reports are written to docs/agent/evidence/S0/reviews/. ADR-0002:43-45 quotes the owner verbatim. findings.harnessRule: Master §0: nothing leaves the local environment until the owner approves it. OPERATIONS §3 and the master §49 owner package say nothing about content.
findings.impact: The first approved push of the integration branch would publish the harness, every log and review, and the owner's own words. Add a publication checklist to the owner package: secret-scan docs/agent, hold security write-ups until their fix is deployed, and decide which of the evidence, reviews and ADRs go public. findings.title: Design §7.4.1's 'no copies' chip reveals hidden Cambodian carriers before the Genetics Lab
findings.evidence: Design:580 says: 'Known from the phenotype (neutral chip, title "The visible trait already proves this"): codominant/additive loci always; mendelian loci when the expressed allele has nothing below it (bottom of ladder) → "2 copies"; otherwise for new-gene loci where no copy is present AND it would be visible → "no copies".' Design:581 defines the Hidden chip '+ ?' ('Second copy hidden until the Genetics Lab'). Design:588: 'Disclosure rule matches the creature card: hidden until `genetics_lab` is unlocked'. Design:496: 'Hidden carriers appear once you research the Genetics Lab.' Cambodian is a mendelian recessive that shows only on red fish (design:664; C has dominance 2 and c has dominance 1, design:691-692). A red betta with a normal body is either C/C or C/c. Applied to the genome, the rule labels C/C 'no copies' with the 'proves' chip and C/c '+ ?'. Applied to the phenotype, it claims 'no copies' for a fish that may carry c. offer-genes.test.ts (design:1441, 'known vs hidden copies') would lock in whichever reading the builder picks.
findings.harnessRule: Design §7.4.1 and §9.1 disclosure rule (hidden until genetics_lab is unlocked). Master S2 'genotype disclosure rules'.
findings.impact: The panel's data source is the genome (offer.creatures[active].genome). Built as written, it lets players tell before the Genetics Lab which red bettas carry Cambodian, which are exactly the fish needed for the new very rare Red Cambodian Veiltail. That undercuts both the lab and the pre-lab rule of the 'Rare genes' filter.
findings.fix: Fix the design through an ADR erratum: before the lab, a mendelian locus whose expressed allele isn't at the bottom of its ladder always shows '+ ?', and 'no copies' appears only after the lab. Add a test that a C/C and a C/c red betta give identical Genes rows and 'Rare genes' results before the lab.

votes.reason: Every cited line exists and says what the finding claims. If you trace the §7.4.1 copies-chip rule against the Cambodian locus data, the panel gives different pre-lab chips to two red bettas that look the same. That breaks the "hidden until genetics_lab" disclosure rule the same section claims to follow (line 588, §9.1). The finding also misses a second, related leak, described below.
votes.fixAssessment:
The proposed fix is right in direction and safe: an ADR erratum plus a test that a C/C red and a C/c red give identical Genes rows and identical Rare genes results before the lab. It is incomplete, though, because it doesn't cover the conditional-locus leak.

Better fix: state the erratum as a general phenotype rule. Before the lab, a copies chip is "known" only when every genotype that fits the visible phenotype gives the same copy count. Everything else shows "+ ?". In practice:
1. Drop the "new-gene ... no copies" clause before the lab. "no copies" for a mendelian locus appears only after the lab.
2. For conditional loci whose condition isn't met (Cambodian on a non-red fish), always show "+ ?", even for c/c.
3. Codominant and additive loci stay "always known".

Tests to add to offer-genes.test.ts:
- Red C/C and red C/c give identical rows.
- Royal c/c and royal C/C give identical rows.
- Red c/c shows "2 copies".
- After the lab, the chips show the true genotype.

For the Rare genes filter, a non-identity check (pre-lab results the same for C/C and C/c red) is a reasonable guard, but the filter's current spec (visible tier/strain only) is not itself broken.

votes.reason:
The finding holds, and the leak is wider than reported. §7.4.1 builds the Copies chip from the genome (`offer.creatures[active].genome`, line 588). Its "known from the phenotype" branch says (line 580): "otherwise for new-gene loci where no copy is present AND it would be visible → 'no copies'". Cambodian is the only new mendelian locus, because Metallic is additive and is already covered by "always". So that clause only ever applies to Cambodian, and it applies by genome: a red C/C fish gets "no copies" with the title "The visible trait already proves this", while a red C/c fish gets "+ ?". The two look the same, so the panel tells them apart before the Genetics Lab, which breaks line 588 ("hidden until `genetics_lab` is unlocked") and the pre-lab promise on line 496. The only reading that doesn't leak is "a single copy would be visible". That is never true for a recessive, so under that reading the clause does nothing, and a builder is unlikely to read it that way.

The reviewer missed a second leak. The Trait column shows "the expressed allele", and the engine's `expressedAlleles` looks at one locus only. It doesn't apply the red-only overlay condition. So a royal-blue c/c fish shows Trait "Cambodian", and because c is at the bottom of the ladder it gets the known "2 copies" chip. That reveals Cambodian on non-red fish, which contradicts §8.1 ("On any other colour it stays hidden") and the §8.4 row "royal/royal · cambodian c/c → Royal Blue … (Cambodian hidden)".

Where this stands now: the current slice is S0 (STATE.json `"currentSlice": "S0"`), and no Genes panel code exists yet. Nothing affects players or saves today. The risk is a future builder agent that follows the approved spec literally, plus `offer-genes.test.ts` (line 1441: "known vs hidden copies"), which would lock that behaviour in. Saves are not affected. The harm is to game balance: buyers could pick out Cambodian carriers before the lab, and those are the parents of the new very rare Red Cambodian Veiltail. Medium severity is right for an approved design that an autonomous builder will carry out word for word.
votes.fixAssessment:
The ADR erratum is the right vehicle, since the spec is owner-approved and should not be edited quietly. As proposed, though, the fix only covers the red C/C vs C/c case. A fuller erratum:
(1) Remove the "no copies" sub-clause from the "known from the phenotype" branch. Before the lab, "no copies" never appears for a mendelian locus.
(2) The pre-lab Trait and Copies chip for a mendelian locus come from what the phenotype shows, not from the genome alone. For a conditional locus (Cambodian) whose condition isn't met (the fish is not showing red), show the top allele's name ("Normal body") with the "only shows on red bettas" summary and a hidden chip. Never show "Cambodian / 2 copies" on a non-red fish.
(3) Only a bottom-of-ladder allele that actually shows (its overlay applies) gets the known "2 copies" chip.
(4) Tests in offer-genes.test.ts: before the lab, red C/C and red C/c give identical Genes rows, and royal C/C and royal c/c give identical Genes rows. After the lab, all four show their true copies. Add matching shop-filters.test.ts cases for the "Rare genes" filter.
One related point to check in the same ADR: the §7.2 hidden-carrier rule ("rare allele NOT expressed in its phenotype"), if built on the engine's `expressedAlleles`, would treat royal c/c as "expressed". It would then leave that fish out of "Rare genes" even after the lab. "Expressed" should mean "shown in the resolved morph" (the overlay applied).

findings.title: A crash anywhere in the in-game HUD leaves the aquarium running and autosaving with no way to pause: the S06-06 pause covers only the outer 'interface' boundary
findings.evidence: ErrorBoundary.tsx:4-6 says: 'the game loop lives outside every boundary, so after an interface crash the aquarium kept running and autosaving behind a blank HUD with no way to pause ... The fallback now pauses the clock'. But :29 pauses only `if (this.props.name === 'interface')`, and :58 shows 'Your aquarium is paused' only for 'interface'. App.tsx:79-82 wraps UIRoot in the 'interface' boundary and keeps <GameLoop /> outside it. UIRoot.tsx:69-71 wraps <GameHUD /> in its own `<ErrorBoundary name="hud">`, which catches HUD errors first. GameHUD contains the TopBar with SpeedControls (:343), every panel through PanelHost (:385-388) and the Space-to-pause handler (:184 `togglePause()`). There are no global error handlers, and no test references ErrorBoundary.
findings.harnessRule: Master §6: don't regress existing strengths (persistent saves and resilience fixes). The S06-06 fix is documented but untested, and it no longer applies to the main HUD.
findings.impact: A crash in any panel, the dock, the tool rail or the top bar replaces the whole HUD. The clock keeps running at the chosen speed and autosaves keep writing. With the controls and the hotkey gone, the player can't pause, so animals can starve or die before they reload. Known triggers exist: the listed Settings crash happens inside a separate 'settings' boundary that doesn't pause either, and a missing lazy chunk (next finding) lands here.
findings.fix: Pause the clock in componentDidCatch for every in-game boundary (at least 'hud' and 'settings') and show the paused line there too. Add a test that throws inside GameHUD and asserts clock.speed === 0.

votes.reason: The finding's main claim is false. The 'hud' boundary in UIRoot is not the S06-06 boundary in src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx. UIRoot.tsx:11 imports `{ ErrorBoundary } from './common/ErrorBoundary'`, which is a separate lane component (src/ui/common/ErrorBoundary.tsx). Inside GameHUD, every section has its own fine-grained boundary: topbar (:342), tankbar, tools, roomcam, toolhint, dock, tutorial, party, creature-card, tank-card, panels (:386, with PanelErrorBoundary inside PanelHost), photo and welcome. So a crash in a panel, the dock, the tool rail or the top bar blanks only that section. GameHUD stays mounted, and so does its useHudKeys Space-to-pause handler (:180-185), so the player can still pause. For a panel crash, PanelErrorBoundary also shows "Try again" and "Close". A Settings crash blanks only Settings, and the HUD and hotkeys keep working. The statement "a crash in any panel, the dock, the tool rail or the top bar replaces the whole HUD" is therefore wrong. A smaller residual gap is real. A throw in GameHUD's own body or hooks, or in WatchRestore (which has no boundary of its own), is caught by the outer ui/common 'hud' boundary. That boundary renders null after only a console.warn: the HUD disappears with no message and no pause, and the game loop and autosave keep running. That is a low-severity issue, not the medium-severity one described.
votes.fixAssessment: The proposed fix targets the wrong component. Changing the name check in src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx to include 'hud' and 'settings' would do nothing, because UIRoot's 'hud' and 'settings' boundaries are instances of src/ui/common/ErrorBoundary.tsx. Pausing on every sub-section crash, such as the topbar or a single panel, is also unnecessary, because the Space hotkey and the other controls survive those crashes. A better, minimal fix is to use the app-level boundary (src/app/ErrorBoundary) for the outer 'hud' wrapper in UIRoot.tsx:69, or to give the ui/common 'hud' boundary a visible fallback that pauses the clock through useGame.getState().mutate, the same way 'interface' does. That way a throw in GameHUD's own body, useHudKeys or WatchRestore shows a message, pauses the game and offers Save & reload instead of a silent blank HUD. Add a test that throws inside GameHUD's body and asserts clock.speed === 0 and that the alert is visible. A second test should throw inside TopBar and assert that the rest of the HUD and the Space-to-pause hotkey still work.

votes.reason:
There is a real gap, but it is much smaller than reported, and the finding misreads the code. UIRoot and GameHUD do not use src/app/ErrorBoundary. They import a different class, src/ui/common/ErrorBoundary, which renders nothing when it catches an error. Also, every HUD section (topbar, dock, tools, panels and so on) has its own boundary. A crash in a panel, the dock, the tool rail or the top bar therefore removes only that section, not the whole HUD. The Space-to-pause handler (useHudKeys, which lives in GameHUD) keeps working, and a panel crash shows PanelErrorBoundary's "This panel hit a snag" card with a Close button. The two "known triggers" don't reach the 'hud' boundary either. 'settings' is a sibling of 'hud' in UIRoot, and a lazy PanelHost or PhotoMode chunk that fails to load is caught by the 'panels' or 'photo' boundary. What remains true:
- Only the App-level 'interface' boundary pauses.
- An error in GameHUD's own body (its hooks useHudKeys, usePopoverDismiss, useCardDockRules and the rest, the motion.div wrapper, or the unwrapped WatchRestore) trips the UIRoot 'hud' boundary. That boundary silently renders null: no message, no pause, no reload button. The clock and autosave keep running, and the Space handler is unmounted.
- A topbar crash silently removes the visible pause and speed controls. Space and keys 1-3 still work, but nothing tells the player that.
- No test covers any boundary.
No concrete trigger for a GameHUD-level crash is known. The severity is low, not medium.
votes.fixAssessment:
The proposed fix targets the wrong class. Adding 'hud' and 'settings' to the name check in src/app/ErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch would change nothing, because those boundaries are instances of src/ui/common/ErrorBoundary. Pausing on a 'settings' crash isn't needed either: the HUD and its pause controls stay up. Pausing on every section crash would be too broad; a crash in a portrait or the party banner shouldn't stop the game.

A better fix:
1. Use src/app/ErrorBoundary (which pauses and offers Save & reload) for UIRoot's 'hud' boundary. Alternatively, add an opt-in `pauseOnCrash` prop and a visible fallback to src/ui/common/ErrorBoundary and set both on 'hud' only.
2. Give 'topbar' a small fallback that keeps a pause button visible, or have it pause the game when it crashes.
3. Wrap WatchRestore in a boundary.
4. Add a vitest or RTL test that mocks a GameHUD-level hook to throw. It should assert that useGame.getState().game.clock.speed === 0 and that the fallback alert renders.

This is UI-only and doesn't touch the simulation, so it raises no determinism concerns. It is a core-owned file change under master §3.8, so it needs a slice and an independent review.

findings.title: Design §6.6 share links point at per-save counter ids, so a shared link shows 'gone' or opens someone's unrelated object
findings.evidence: Design:73 lists 'shareable links to offers' as a 0.5 goal. Design:305: '... so a shared link never lands on nothing'. Design:340: 'Real ids are opaque, for example `tank_k2x`, `cr_9fq`, `offer_k3x9` and `listing_7mm`'. §6.6 (:445-452) adds Copy link and the system share sheet. In the code, ids.ts:4-7 does `state.idCounter += 1; return `${prefix}_${state.idCounter.toString(36)}``. newGame.ts:103 starts every save at `idCounter: 0`, and shop.ts:278 gives offers `nextId(state, 'offer')`. Design §6.4 item 3 resolves a link by loading the opener's latest save and then applying the route.
findings.harnessRule: Master §7-§8: the approved design must be buildable as specified. Design §6 routing contract.
findings.impact: Ids are neither opaque nor global: every save counts from the same number. A link sent to another player, or opened in another slot or browser, shows 'This offer has gone' or a different offer that reused the number. Tank and creature links open the recipient's own tank_1 or an unrelated animal. Offers also expire within hours, so the headline share feature can't work as the design describes.
findings.fix: Owner decides what sharing is for. Then either share links that mean the same thing for everyone (a species, morph or catalog entry), or tag links with the save id and show 'This link is from another aquarium' when they don't match. Correct design:340.

votes.reason: The citations are accurate and the main point holds. Ids come from a counter in each save, and the 0.5 design has no server, so an offer link copied in one save cannot resolve to the same offer for another player, another slot or another browser. But the finding overstates the impact. Copy link is specified only on offer detail (§6.6), not on tanks or creatures. For a cross-save offer link, the usual result is the 'This offer has gone' state, which the design already specifies (§6.2 row: 'Unknown or expired → "This offer has gone"'; §6.5; §7.6). A wrong-object hit needs the recipient to have an offer in stock under that exact counter value, and the counter is shared by every prefix (tank, cr, offer and so on), so this is uncommon. The genuine defects are: (a) a link opened in another save can silently show a different object, most clearly tank links, because createTank runs first in every new game and so every save has tank_1; (b) the design never says who shared links are for, while it offers the system share sheet; (c) 'opaque' at design:340 suggests a global or random id, which the code does not produce. This is a design gap in a feature that has not been built, and it degrades safely in most cases, so it is low rather than medium.
votes.fixAssessment: Sending this to the owner as a decision is right, because what sharing is for in 0.5 is a product choice. The proposed fix is safe because it is a design-text change and touches no code. The best fix is the smaller option: add the saveId, or a short hash of it, to shared URLs as a query parameter or hash suffix (e.g. `#/shop/fish/offer_k3x9?s=<hash>`). When it doesn't match the loaded save, show 'This link is from another aquarium' and fall back to the panel's list view. Also reword design:340 to say ids are save-local and must not be parsed, rather than 'opaque'. Do not change nextId to random or global ids: ids.ts is core-owned, simulation ids must stay deterministic under the master's rules, and changing them would break replay and test expectations. If the owner wants links that work for other players, they can only point at save-independent things (species, morph or catalog entry) until a server exists. Same-device use, such as notification deep links and bookmarks, works as specified until the offer expires.

votes.reason: The citations are accurate. Ids are per-save sequential counters, and nothing in the design says who a "shareable link to an offer" is for. So a link sent to another player, or opened against another save, cannot point at the same offer. Under the impact lens, though, the finding overstates the harm. The design already sends unknown ids to a graceful state (§6.5 and §7.6 "This offer has gone", plus a new "See what's in stock" button), so nothing crashes or corrupts. Copy link is specified only on the offer detail (§6.6), not on tanks or creatures, so the "opens the recipient's own tank_1 or an unrelated animal" scenario is outside the designed surface. An offer-id collision needs the recipient's counter to have handed that exact number to an offer that is still in stock. That is possible but rare, and the result is a harmless wrong offer view. The game is single-player with no server (master :677 needs owner approval for shared or cloud features), so no id scheme could make "the same offer" exist for another player. The real defect is that the design never states the audience for a shared link, so the feature looks like it promises more than a local game can deliver. That is a low-severity design clarity gap, not a medium buildability defect. A builder can implement §6.6 exactly as written and it will behave as §6.5 and §7.6 specify.
votes.fixAssessment: An owner decision is the right route, but the scope should be smaller than the finding suggests. Global or content-based ids can't help, because another player's shop does not contain the same offer, so the "species, morph or catalog entry" option only fits if the owner wants links meant for others. The cheapest safe fix is to add one line to design §6.6 saying offer links reopen this save's offer (for the same player and device, notifications and bookmarks) and that after expiry or in another save they show §7.6. If the owner wants links to be shared between players, add an optional save tag built from the existing `state.saveId` (for example `#/shop/fish/offer_k3x9?s=<saveId>` or a hash segment), and show "This link is from another aquarium" plus "See what's in stock" when the tag doesn't match. The router reads only the hash (§6.4 item 6), so the tag must live inside the hash. It must also stay compatible with the `shareUrl` rule of no query flags and with the nav-routes round-trip test in §20. Rewording design:340 is optional: "opaque" there means "don't parse" and does no harm. Changing it to "opaque, per-save" would be clearer. Do not change `nextId`. It is core-owned, deterministic, and save-compatible.

findings.title: A deploy deletes the lazily loaded HUD chunks, so a tab still on the previous build fails into the HUD error boundary
findings.evidence: GameHUD.tsx:15 (`const PanelHost = lazy(() => import('../panels/PanelHost')...`) and :17 (PhotoMode) produce separate chunks; the local build has dist/assets/PanelHost-jb9ajebh.js, PanelHost-DaG7M3Gy.css and PhotoMode-BJq88zh9.js. src has no `vite:preloadError` handler. ErrorBoundary.tsx:39 (`retry = () => this.setState({ error: null })`) re-renders the same module-level lazy component, and React.lazy keeps a rejected import, so 'Try again' throws again. updateCheck.ts:15 polls only every 5 minutes. Both Pages (upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages) and Render publish a whole new dist, so the previous build's hashed chunks disappear.
findings.harnessRule: Release readiness (REL requirements). Master §6: saves and resilience must not regress.
findings.impact: Two cases fail after a deploy: a tab left on the title screen (PanelHost loads when the game screen mounts), and a tab that opens Photo mode for the first time. Either gets 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module'. The 'hud' boundary then replaces the HUD without pausing (previous finding), and only 'Save & reload' recovers.
findings.fix: Handle `vite:preloadError` by saving, then reloading or showing the update prompt. Make 'Try again' recreate the lazy component. Add this case to the 0.5 release checklist; it can stay in the backlog until releases resume.

votes.reason: The main defect is real. PanelHost and PhotoMode are code-split chunks that are not preloaded, nothing in src handles chunk-load failures, React.lazy keeps a rejected import, and both deploy paths publish a whole new dist, so a tab still on the previous build cannot fetch those chunks once a new build goes out. The finding's failure path is wrong, though. It cites src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx and says the 'hud' boundary takes over, with 'Try again' failing and only 'Save & reload' recovering. GameHUD actually imports a different boundary, src/ui/common/ErrorBoundary.tsx, and wraps each lazy component in its own boundary with no fallback, which renders null. The HUD stays up and no error message or buttons appear. Panels and Photo mode just silently do nothing until the page reloads. The 'previous finding' it relies on (the hud boundary replacing the HUD without pausing) does not apply here. Small detail: the repo HEAD is c774d38 on agent/aquariumgo-local-stack-20261005, not 0d9fc5a.
votes.fixAssessment:
The fix direction is right, but parts of it target the wrong component. In order:

1. Add a `window.addEventListener('vite:preloadError', ...)` handler early in main.tsx. It should call event.preventDefault(), flush a save with saveCurrentGame('auto', { flush: true, toast: false }), skip the save for showcase games, then either reload once or show the existing UpdatePrompt. Guard against a reload loop with a sessionStorage flag inside try/catch.
2. 'Make Try again recreate the lazy component' does not apply as written, because the lazy chunks sit under src/ui/common/ErrorBoundary, which has no Try again button. Either wrap the import factory with a retry that, after a failure, re-imports with a cache-busting query or triggers the update prompt, or give the 'panels' and 'photo' boundaries a visible fallback that offers Reload. Without that, the player sees panels silently do nothing.
3. Optionally keep the previous build's /assets on deploy. Render cannot do this easily; Pages would need the earlier artifact merged in. This is more complex than item 1 and not required.

Adding the case to the 0.5 release checklist and holding it in the backlog until releases resume is reasonable at low severity. Any change to src/app or main.tsx is a core-owned edit that needs an approved slice under the harness.

- `context-pack.mjs:58` writes only `repairAttempt` into the State block of the pack, not `repairTarget` or `repairTotalAttempts`.
